Purcell Memorial Center for Exceptional Children Donate Today About us The Father Purcell Memorial Exceptional Children’s Center (FPM) is a skilled pediatric nursing home for 58 developmentally disabled children. It serves children throughout the U.S. of all races and creeds, providing custodial care, medical treatment and rehabilitation programs. The mission of FPM is to provide a residential care program to developmentally disabled children, their families and the larger community without regard to race, color, religion, nationality or socioeconomic status. We exist to serve the nursing, medical, physical and psychological needs of children who, because of severe developmental disabilities, require ongoing residential care in a skilled nursing facility. Our goal is to help each child living at our facility reach their potential and live their life to the fullest. We also strive to serve as an inviting and supportive resource for families. Father Purcell Memorial Exceptional Children's Center (FPM) is a skilled pediatric nursing facility that provides a loving home to 58 developmentally disabled children. Criteria for admission includes, but is not limited to the following: The child must • be in need of 24 hour skilled nursing care • not have an active or chronic communicable disease • not be ventilator dependent Parents considering admission of their child to our facility are encouraged to schedule a visit. clean_text: Home Our History Services Admission Contact Us ||| Search Search Home Our History Services Admission Contact Us Our History Father Harold Purcell came to Montgomery, Alabama in 1934 and founded The City of St. Jude. A center for disabled children was one of Father Purcell’s final dreams for the St. Jude campus. He recognized the need for a quality, loving and long-term care institution that would serve the health and social well-being of children with severe physical disabilities. During his time, no other such program existed in Alabama, and even today there is only one other program. This lack of service prevented many disabled children and their families from receiving the medical care, support and attention they required. Father Purcell did not live to complete this dream but his supporters and the community took it on and finished his work, opening the facility in 1958. The Order of Christian Initiation of Adults (OCIA) is the process established for the universal Church for individuals to become Catholic and receive the sacraments of initiation — Baptism, Confirmation, and the Eucharist. This initiation process also involves a parish community experiencing a renewal in faith as it prepares and welcomes new members into the Church. The Order speaks of conversion as a "spiritual journey." Centered on fostering a deep relationship with Jesus and the Church He founded, this journey takes place through distinct stages over a period of time suitable to bring about a thorough catechesis, significant experience of the parish community, and commitment to the liturgical and moral life of the Catholic faithful. The OCIA process is a restoration of the ancient catechumenate, arising within the first three centuries following the era of the apostles. It was the early Church's way of Christianizing the pagan Roman Empire. The Second Vatican Council called for the restoration and use of this venerable and powerful method of initiation for the worldwide Church. Who is OCIA for? 1. Persons in need of Baptism. 2. Persons baptized in another Christian tradition who desire to become Catholic. 3. Persons baptized Catholic in need of First Communion and/or Confirmation. How did a person become Catholic before OCIA? At most parishes, the person was given individual instruction by the parish priest, or someone delegated by him. Why the change? There were limitations to private instruction. The priest was the only member of the Catholic community with whom the inquirer had contact, apart from any supporting family and friends. Private instruction did not ensure that the inquirer had a lived experience of the Catholic faith, or was exposed to authentic Christian charity as lived in a parish community. Classes begin in August each year. Parents have the first responsibility for the education of their children in the faith, prayer, and all the virtues. They have the duty to provide as far as possible for the physical and spiritual needs of their children. Register for a Sacrament Funerals About this Sacrament Confirmation is one of the three sacraments of initiation for Catholics. It is a sacrament of mature Christian commitment and a deepening of the baptismal gifts. Confirmation is administered by laying on of hands and anointing with chrism accompanied by prayer. The effect of the sacrament of Confirmation is for the individual to be sealed with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Receiving the Sacrament Our Confirmation program begins in the 10th grade year; students are confirmed in their 11th grade year. To schedule events or activities in the Parish Hall or Library, please contact the parish office. Please not that there is a fee for use of the facility if it is not a parish function. At no time is alcohol allowed on parish grounds or facilities. Holy Spirit Parish does not allow any non-registered person to rent any room on the facility GET FINANCIAL HELP OR FOOD? Unfortunately we do not offer assistance from the parish. However, we do suggest that you reach out to our St. Vincent de Paul Ministry. Call them at 334-235-5976. Or, you can call Catholic Social Services at 288-8890. CSS is located at 4455 Narrow Lane Road. CSS offer many services. PUT SOMEONE ON THE PRAYER LIST? We have 2 ways to spread the word when asking for prayers. Our prayer line is a chain that reaches out to those who whish to pray for one another. Please contact Maureen Moore at 279-5848. If you would like to place someone on the prayer list in the bulletin, please contact Karen in the parish office, 277-5631. HAVE A MASS SCHEDULED FOR SOMEONE? A Mass intention can be scheduled for anyone alive or deceased. Call or come by the parish office to schedule one. We will be happy to send a card to someone letting them know a Mass is scheduled. It is customary to donate $10 for each Mass Intention, which goes directly to the priest when it is said. SET UP A TIME TO RECEIVE THE SACRAMENT OF ANOINTING OF THE SICK? In the event of serious illness, death or other sacramental emergency, please call the parish office, 277-5631. Parishioners who anticipate having surgery are strongly encouraged to arrange to receive this anointing before they enter the hospital. Karen will be happy to arrange a time. MAKE AN APPOINTMENT TO SEE A PRIEST? Call the parish office, 277-5631. Karen will be happy to set up a time for you to come in to meet with Fr. Monteron and Fr. Francis. If you need a priest to come visit with you in your home, give us a call. 8570 Vaughn Road, Montgomery, AL 36117Tel: 334-277-5631 Facebook Instagram Email Phone Login powered by eCatholic ®

Register for a Sacrament Funerals At Holy Spirit Parish preparation for First Holy Communion is during second grade. Students will prepare either at school (if they attend Montgomery Catholic Preparatory School) or in our Children’s Faith Formation program. In both instances, First Reconciliation is prepared for and celebrated first semester and First Holy Communion is prepared for and celebrated second semester. (To register in our Children’s Faith Formation classes, click here) Faith Formation classes are offered Sundays from 9:30am – 10:30am (see calendar) If your child is in need of these sacraments out of these scheduled preparation years, we have options. One of those is a special RCIA adapted for children class. Please contact us if your child is in need of preparation. (Schedule is different than what is posted below) Important Dates For First Reconciliation and First Holy Communion First Reconciliation Parent Meeting (1 parent must attend): Sunday, September 29, 2025 at 9:45 in the school gym First Reconciliation: Saturday, December 7, 2024 First Communion Parent Meeting (1 parent must attend): Sunday, January 26, 2025 at 9:45am in the school gym First Communion Retreat Morning: Sunday, April 27, 2025 First Holy Communion: Saturday, May 3, 2025 at 2:00pm Director: Zavie George Email: [email protected] Dressing for First Communion Boys Dress slacks. Button-down white dress shirt and tie. Suits, sport coats, or a vest. Socks must be worn with appropriate dress shoes. Students will not be permitted to carry anything (prayer books, rosary beads, etc.) into the sanctuary or during their First Communion but may have them for professional photographs. Girls White dress. Sleeveless dresses are ok; no strapless tops or spaghettis straps. Wide straps are okay. If you need to cover shoulders, a shrug is suggested. Socks or stockings should be worn. Appropriate white dress shoes – if sandals they must have a strap in the back and no high heels or wedges – they must have flat bottoms. No purses or gloves during Mass but can be in pictures. Veils are encouraged; no hats, please. Veils and/or ribbons from the headpiece should be manageable for your daughter. WARNING: Sprayed in sparkles or glitter can flake into a girl’s eyes and cause distress and tears. Students will not be permitted to carry anything (prayer books, rosary beads, etc.) during their First Communion but may have them for professional photographs. Register for a Sacrament Funerals Funerals The sadness of death should give way in our liturgy to the promise of resurrected life. Our celebration of a person's life should reflect our conviction that is Jesus Christ we have life beyond life. Holy Spirit offers a funeral Mass as a means of consolation for the living and grace-filled assistance for the deceased. Once you have contacted the funeral home, you may contact Karen Franklin in the parish office by calling 334-277-5631. She will set up an appointment to meet with your family. Dinner is provided at 6:45pm in the Parish Hall followed by faith-building games and discussions that encourage teens to grow in their faith through worship, fellowship and service. Worship activities include: Mass, monthly Adoration and Confession. Weekly Activities may include: Peer faith talks, peer led discussion groups, fellowship building games, small groups, Apologetics Nights Faith Building Retreats and Fellowship may include: Archdiocese Search Retreat, ACYC (Archdiocese Youth Conference) Retreat, March for Life in Washington D.C., and Parish Youth Group Retreats. Adult Volunteers: Help is needed with food preparation on Sunday evenings and occasional set-up and break down. Adults are also needed for small group discussions chaperones are also helpful for youth trips and retreats. For more information, contact Sarah, Confirmation Coordinator. [email protected] Confirmation Our Confirmation program begins in the students 10th grade year and confirmed in their 11th grade year. For more information, contact Sarah Rose Burden at [email protected] About this Sacrament Confirmation is one of the three sacraments of initiation for Catholics. It is a sacrament of mature Christian commitment and a deepening of the baptismal gifts. Confirmation is administered by laying on of hands and anointing with chrism accompanied by prayer. The effect of the sacrament of Confirmation is for the individual to be sealed with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Receiving the Sacrament Our Confirmation program begins in the the 10th grade year; students are confirmed in their 11th grade year. As such, we are proud to be a part of the world’s largest Catholic family fraternal service organization. We embrace the four principles of our order as established by our founder, Father Michael J. McGivney: Charity, Unity, Fraternity, and Patriotism. We provide aid for those in need and we support the right to life and work to make our church and community a better place for all. Membership is open to all men over the age of 18 who are practicing Catholics. Activities Council 12150 meets the second Monday of every month in the Parish Hall at 7:00 p.m. Our activities include: monthly parish breakfast, annual Father & Daughter Valentine’s Day dance, support of several local charities, blood drives, special meals, assist with parish picnic, Knights of Columbus night at Riverwalk Stadium with the Montgomery Biscuits, and family activities. Training is provided on how to care for the special altar linens that contain the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. This ministry is made up of team members who, in their own homes, reverently launder and care for the purificators and corporals used on the altar at Mass. Time commitment – members serve on a rotating basis throughout the year. Depending on the number of volunteers, a volunteer may launder altar linens 3-4 times a year, or less. Contact: Arleen Alexander [email protected] Altar Servers · Altar Servers serve the priest at the altar, setting an example for parishioners how to participate in the Mass by joyfully singing and responding. Children in grades 3 (who have made their 1st Communion) through high school, may be altar servers. · Training is required and will be provided after signing up as a volunteer. · Altar servers are scheduled for Sunday Masses and Solemnities or Holy Days of Obligation based on their availability and the need. There are also instances where they may need to serve for weddings, funerals, and other special liturgies. Arleen Alexander [email protected] Audio-Visual Ministry The Ministry is responsible for set-up, maintenance, coordination and operation of the church’s audiovisual technology used during masses, programs and other special events.. Volunteers will be scheduled and training will be provided. Experience with sound systems is not required, but if you have such experience, please consider volunteering. John Klein: ​ [email protected] Extraordinary Ministers of Holy Communion · The Extraordinary Ministers of Holy Communion (EMHCs) assist the priest with the distribution of Holy Communion. · EMHCs must be approved and complete required training before serving. Names of EMHCs are submitted to the archbishop. · EMHCs are scheduled for Sunday Masses and Solemnities or Holy Days of Obligation, based on their availability and the need. Arleen Alexander [email protected] Floral Committee The Holy Spirit Floral Committee works to create a welcoming, and esthetically pleasing environment that promotes the intent of the liturgy and heightens our encounter with God. The presence of plants/flowers symbolizes Christ’s victory over death. Our purpose is to enrich the spiritual environment for the entire church membership. This is accomplished by beautifying the church with plants and flowers using (real and silk stems) on Sundays, and other liturgical worship seasons. The members of this committee are presented with a calendar, for each liturgical season in order to create the two Sunday altar arrangements throughout the year. (There are no altar arrangements during Advent and Lent). We work in pairs to create these arrangements once every 5-6 weeks. In addition, we all come together to decorate the church for Easter Sunday. (Fresh flowers are always used for Easter Sunday). We are a very small committee but have a big love for what we have been called to do! We pray you will be called too! ​Shirley Garrett [email protected] or Bonnie McClure [email protected] Lectors · Lectors, or readers, proclaim Sacred Scripture on Sunday Masses and HolyDays of Obligation, during the Liturgy of the Word. · Training is required and will be provided after signing up as a volunteer. · Lectors are scheduled for Sunday Masses and Solemnities or Holydays of Obligation, based on their availability and the need. Arleen Alexander [email protected] Music Ministry As an essential liturgical ministry, the music team at Holy Spirit Parish seeks to foster and develop the full, conscious, and active participation of the gathered congregation at each of our weekly liturgies and Holy Days throughout the year. The music ministry at Holy Spirit offers a different character at each of our four weekend liturgies. Music at our Saturday evening mass is led by a cantor. Our two Sunday morning liturgies have a choir mid-August through Pentecost, with cantors and small groups leading during the remaining summer months. These ensembles primarily use the Journeysongs hymnal, found in the pews. Finally, our Sunday evening mass has a contemporary ensemble which focuses on repertoire of current and active composers like Matt Maher, Scott Soper, and others of similar style. Choir rehearsal is on Wednesday nights at 7 PM during the choir season. Additionally, each of the mass groups meet before their weekly mass to prepare for the upcoming liturgy: the 8 am choir meets at 7:30 the 11 am choir meets at 10:15. The contemporary ensemble meets at 4 pm on Sundays and the cantor and accompanist for the Saturday evening mass coordinate their own rehearsal time. We are always looking to expand involvement in the program–singers and instrumentalists of any experience and skill level are welcome–including high school and college students. Please contact us here. We are especially in need of experienced service players to serve as accompanists at mass. We have both hired and volunteer opportunities available. Ushers · An Usher is a minister of hospitality in the parish. Usher, as the ones who stand at the door, greet, and distribute bulletins, are the ambassadors for the parish, and a have key part in the body of Christ. Duties of Ushers include, but are not limited to: welcoming and door-keeping, seating for Mass, collections, clean-up after Mass. · Serving as an Usher is also a great way to get to know your parish family through assisting them on a regular basis. · Training is required and will be provided after signing up as a volunteer. · Ushers are scheduled for Sunday Masses and Solemnities or Holydays of Obligation, based on their availability and the need. (Children age-out at 5 years old). Teacher-Child Ratio : 1:3 First come, first served. Maximum Capacity: 9 Children Mission Statement We welcome the children of our community into a safe, positive, inviting, and enriching environment while encouraging each child to encounter Jesus, the Good Shepherd, in our Montessori inspired nursery. The nursery is available for children ages 12 months through four years old. You MUST fill out a registration form for each child attending the nursery. Please stop by the nursery, parish office, or print the forms linked below. Parents and guardians may leave a child in the nursery ONLY to attend Mass or an event at Holy Spirit Parish. You must remain on campus at one of the listed events while your child is in the nursery: Sunday morning 7:45am-12:15pm (for 8am Mass, 9:15am-10:45am Children and Adult Faith Formation & RCIA, and 11am Mass) The First Friday of the month 5:15pm-7:45pm (for First Friday Family Adoration; Begins in September) Other occasional events as advertised in the bulletin or requested by organizations. The nursery is staffed with both paid employees and volunteers. All employees are CPR and First Aid certified, have successfully completed a required background check, and have completed Child Protection training through the Archdiocese of Mobile. Adults are welcome to volunteer in the Nursery. Parents/Guardians are encouraged to do so as they are able. All adult volunteers must have a background check and be Child Protection trained in the Archdiocese of Mobile. Teens over the age of 12 are also permitted to volunteer in the nursery as a Teen Aide after undergoing training. Contact the Nursery Supervisor to volunteer and arrange training. 8570 Vaughn Road, Montgomery, AL 36117Tel: 334-277-5631 Facebook Instagram Email Phone Login powered by eCatholic ®

May on June 10, 1977 with the appointment of Rev. Gordon Milsted as pastor. The first parish Mass was celebrated on June 19th at the library on the high school campus of the Montgomery Catholic Preparatory School. The 87 charter parish families continued to worship at that site while plans for permanent church grounds and structure were made. Father Milsted took up residence at the St. Bede rectory until December of the following year when a house located in the Brighton Estates neighborhood was purchased for that purpose. Vaugn Road Parish Campus Purchased September, 1979 In September of 1979, 14.3 acres of land located at the current Vaughn Road parish campus was purchased. Groundbreaking ceremonies for a new church building were held in March of 1980, and on the following November 16th the newly ordained Archbishop Oscar Hugh Lipscomb dedicated the church and was the main celebrant for the first Mass in the new church, a day which coincided with his installation as the first Archbishop of Mobile. The project was completed with seating for 300 in the church proper in addition to a small kitchen and large multi-purpose room. A small house purchased with the land was kept for meeting and classroom space and was designated as Thomas Hall, named in honor of Thomas Germanson, the chairman of the Building Committee. In March of 1985, a new rectory built on the parish grounds was dedicated. Fr. Charles Troncale was appointed Pastor September 2, 1999 Fr. Charles Troncale was appointed Pastor on September 2, 1999. The parish broke ground on a new 758-seat church on December 5, 1999, with the dedication by Archbishop Lipscomb to follow on May 12th of 2001. In February 2000, the 5.3 acres bordering the church property to the south were purchased from parishioner Helena Malus. A house located on the purchased property was remodeled and became the new rectory in March of 2002. In 2005, the former rectory was remodeled to serve as parish offices. Fr. Patrick Driscoll appointed Pastor On May 29, 2011 On May 29, 2011, it was announced that Fr. Patrick Driscoll was to become the new pastor of the parish effective the following October 15, replacing Fr. Troncale who was going to St. Vincent de Paul parish in Tallassee. On July 16, 2011, the parish broke ground on a project which involved both construction of the first phase of an education complex and significant site improvements to the property. On August 12, 2012, Archbishop Thomas John Rodi dedicated the new two-story, twenty-one classroom building. In addition to parish catechetical classes and religious education programs, the new building houses the Holy Spirit campus of the Montgomery Catholic Preparatory School and consists of classes ranging from K4 through 6th grade. Church Features & Symbolism The Altar The new altar design brings the tabernacle to the center of the sanctuary. The Tabernacle The tabernacle design is based on the historic Ark of the Covenant which housed the original Ten Commandments. A Catholic tabernacle houses the Blessed Sacrament, Jesus Christ as the new Covenant in Eucharistic form. This one is silk-lined and hand-crafted from acacia wood by artist Gianfranco Tassara of Milwaukee. It is located in the Blessed Sacrament Chapel which is reminiscent of the “Holy of Holies” in the Temple of the Old Testament. A red sanctuary lamp marks the presence of the Eucharist. The table supporting the tabernacle projects from the chapel wall and is topped with rare white limestone. Tabernacle doors are embossed with diamonds and flanked by brass panels, one depicting the Biblical raining of manna in the desert and the other representing the hosts and wheat of the Eucharist. Poles across the top of the tabernacle represent the tools with which the Ark of the Covenant was carried and the molding around the top is designed to reflect the concentric circles of the complimenting candlesticks. Resting atop of the tabernacle are hand-carved Ecuadorian angels posturing adoration. Baptismal Font The altar design conveys multiple meanings. The chosen material, Rosa of Salome marble, is solid, polished rock, strong enough to be an “altar of sacrifice”. The marble was excavated in Italy especially for this church project and was selected for its reddish brown streaks, calling to mind the blood of the sacrificial Lamb. The base is shaped like a cross while the top represents the table at the Last Supper where Christ initiated his own incarnation in the Eucharist. There are five crosses carved into the altar surface. Positioned in the entryway, the baptismal font serves as a central location for holy water as well as a reminder of the baptismal sacrament. The upper bowl shape is reminiscent of Noah’s Ark and the vessel which carried Moses safely down the river. The white marble symbolizes purification. The lower font is made of earthy sandstone, setting off the white of the marble rising from it. Water taken from the upper font would be used to baptize a person standing down in the sandstone, with the person subsequently rising “up out of the water” (cf. Romans: 3-6) after baptism. The overall circular design symbolizes the all-encompassing love of God with no beginning or end. The brass spokes on the wheel-shaped base are engraved with the seven sacraments of the Catholic Church. Three upper font plates are engraved with the three virtues flowing from baptism: faith, hope and charity. The Ceiling of Prayers Over 100 volunteers hand-painted 2600 acoustical tiles to complete the 10,000 square foot ceiling artwork. The re wrapping process prevented the original intent of having names and prayers written on the backs of tiles as they face up to God, but many silent prayers helped shape the ceiling project. Each tile was spray-painted gold, then repackaged and delivered to a design site in the pastor’s house behind the church. Parishioners then sponge- painted crimson, violet, purple, and emerald liturgical colors onto the tiles, making each one unique and yet integral to an overall design by artist Susan Marie Pieri. Approximately 35% of the tiles had to be measured and hand-cut to fit the final grid. Each golden diamond pattern measures four feet by 2 feet, the same dimensions as each tablet containing the Ten Commandments. 8570 Vaughn Road, Montgomery, AL 36117Tel: 334-277-5631 Facebook Instagram Email Phone Login powered by eCatholic ®

Each November we put up a Christmas tree in the Church gallery that is covered with tags that correspond to the individual agencies that we work with each year. We currently partner several agencies in the River Region: Montgomery County DHR to provide Christmas gifts to babies and children that are being served through Foster Care and Child Protective Services. Catholic Social Services to provide gift cards that are used by their outreach program throughout the year-not just Christmas to support their clientele. Crises pregnancy centers: COPE to provide gift cards and monetary donations that are used throughout the year to support expectant and new moms that come to them for assistance. Mary’s Haven to provide gift cards and monetary donations that are used throughout the year to support expectant and new moms that come to them for assistance. We are always in need of volunteers to aid us each year as we work to ensure the success of this project so that we can help those that need us the most! Contact Elizabeth Gregorius, [email protected] , for more information on volunteer opportunities or to ask questions. Hospitality Committee Come be a part of this dynamic group that supports our Holy Spirit families in times of joy, as well as in times of bereavement. As a group, we bring our parish together through the gift of food. From setting up to the final clean up we provide for a beautiful gathering for receptions, funeral lunches, and a myriad of other occasions. No experience or special talents are required, only a willingness to be open to supporting this ministry. You will be blessed with the friendships that are formed as you become a member of this committee. Contact Anne Ceasar, [email protected] Facilities & Grounds The Facilities and Grounds Ministry help enrich our parish environment with the upkeep of the facilities and grounds. This ministry offers you the ability to use your God given talents to serve others by fulfilling the needs and challenges that the upkeep of a parish offers. Please prayerfully consider joining this ministry. Contact: John Klein [email protected] Family Events Committee Family Events Committee Designed to bring families together for fellowship, fun, and meaningful engagement through activities that strengthen relationships and build a sense of community. We hope to create a fun and safe environment where families can come together and have meaningful moments and memories. We host a variety of events throughout the year such as dances, trivia nights, and fun seasonal activities like trunk-or-treat. Our meetings are scheduled around upcoming events. We gladly welcome helping hands and would love to connect with you about how you can get involved. Contact Jen Denham, [email protected] Knitting & Crocheting Ministry We are pleased that you have chosen to learn more about the Knitting and Crochet Ministry at Holy Spirit Parish. This group blends fellowship with charity, crafting handmade items for those in need in our community while growing closer in faith together. Contact Peggy Comer, [email protected] Senior Spirits Mission The primary mission of the Holy Spirit Senior Spirits group is to provide Social and Spiritual support to its members with church sponsored activities. We accomplish this through regularly scheduled activities that foster relationships within the senior community. We embrace our diversity and are enthusiastic about participating in Parish activities to the extent we are able. Activites We meet for a Fall luncheon, Christmas luncheon and a Saint Patrick’s luncheon. We also support a Parish or local Catholic charity with contributions. We encourage all senior members of our Parish, 50 and older, to join us to help carry out our mission to both socially and spiritually support our Parish and fellow parishioners as they journey through their golden years. Contact: Cindy Russell, [email protected] Seaton Haven Outreach Mission Coordinate birthday parties for residents in Seaton Haven Senior Living Activities Monthly meetings for party arrangement and gift giving. Birthday party and fun games. Donations are always needed for the monthly Birthday Parties. Please place your new or gently used gift items in the basket behind the 10 Commandments wall in the vestibule of the church. Gift Cards are always welcome, please take them to the church office. For more information, contact Pier Geis, [email protected] St. Camillus Members of this ministry, who must be Extrordinary Eucharistic Ministers of Holy Communion from Holy Spirit Parish, bring the Blessed Sacrament (on a rotating basis) to the homebound and to those in nursing facilities on a weekly basis. Friday is the designated day; however, if that is not possible, the Minister of Holy Communion may adjust the day. To join or volunteer contact Karen Franklin, [email protected] Welcoming Committee The Welcome Committee seeks to consistently and personally welcome all newly registered parishioners by connecting them with the resources they need to fully join our Parish. You can get involved by volunteering to help with any or all of our three tasks: contacting each family as they register, handing out welcome bags two weekends in August after each Mass, and hosting a reception for new members in September. Contact Gina Izer, [email protected] 8570 Vaughn Road, Montgomery, AL 36117Tel: 334-277-5631 Facebook Instagram Email Phone Login powered by eCatholic ®

Commit one hour weekly to sitting, praying and listening for the message that Christ will bring to you. Your life will be forever changed and your special hour will become food for your soul and the foundation for your spiritual walk with the Lord. Contact Anne Ceasar, [email protected] Jesus, Mary, and Joseph Adoration Guild The “Jesus, Mary, and Joseph Adoration Guild” at Holy Spirit Parish is a prayer ministry that witnesses to the special bond between the Hearts of Jesus, Mary, and Joseph, i.e. the Holy Family by holding the all-night vigil of Adoration on the First Friday/First Saturday of each month. The second side of this sheet has more details about the reason for the choice of First Friday and First Saturday. For more info, click Here . Men of St. Joseph Mission Spiritual Formation prayer group of Christian men, united under the Catholic Church, who meet regularly to study Sunday Mass readings. The purpose of the Men of St. Joseph is to instill holiness in men and facilitate spiritual leadership in family and community life. Reflection Gospel Insight for men. Creating a Culture of Faith for Family, Church and Community All men college age and above are invited to join in this ongoing prayer group called "Men of Saint Joseph". We will meet from 5:00pm-6:00pm every Wednesday night before the 6:00pm mass in the Library. The format is reading the Gospel for the upcoming Sunday (with accompanying commentary) and then prayerfully reflecting on the Gospel together and sharing our inspired insights. Contact Tom Ohland, [email protected] Mom's Group A group of moms growing together in faith and friendship. Mom group meets in the church nursery on Tuesdays from 9-11am to pray and play together. We also coordinate playdates on other days for those who cannot make the weekly meeting. Please reach out to join our community! Contact Anna Broadwater [email protected] Prayer Line The Prayer Line provides spiritual support, comfort and encouragement through prayers to those who request them. We pray for those in need in all aspects of life; for those of family, friends and our world. We currently have more than 90 prayer warriors on the Holy Spirit Prayer Line. Prayer requests are sent to members of the prayer team, and each member then prays on their own for the request. It’s a very important and rewarding ministry, and updates are shared to see how powerful their prayers have been. There are no meetings, which allows anyone who can’t participate physically to be a very important part of our Church. Contact Maureen Moore, [email protected] Respect Life The Respect Life Ministry works to promote the culture of life in both the parish and the community. In conjunction with respect life month we have a literature outreach to the parish. Our members are also active in setting up the Cemetery of the Innocent display in conjunction with the Roe vs. Wade decision to legalize abortion. We work directly with COPE, a local crisis pregnancy center with our time, talent and donations. An important aspect of our ministry is reaching out to those within our own church who either through lack of knowledge or improper catechesis do not understand the church’s consistent teaching in regard to abortion, euthanasia, living wills, and all other life issues. We are always looking for new people and ideas to promote the gospel of life! Contact: John Klein [email protected] Seven Sisters Apostolate The Seven Sisters Apostolate is a call to strengthen the Church by ensuring that a Holy Hour is prayed each day of the week for the sole intention of a specific Priest or Bishop—a “holy wasting” (see Mt. 26:10) or lavishing of prayer for his deeper conformity to Christ. A Seven Sisters group begins when at least seven women respond to a call to the mission of the apostolate. If more than seven women desire to pray in this manner, a core group of seven should be designated while others may substitute or provide additional hours of prayer. The coordinator of a group is known as the Anchoress . The first recipient of a Seven Sisters group should always be their parish Priest. After the Priest has a committed group, subsequent groups may be formed for others, such as the parochial vicar, a retired priest, a priest serving in a non-parish assignment, or a Bishop. The group’s intention is directed towards the office of the shepherd more than the individual. In other words, the group prays for that particular priest until he is reassigned, at which time his successor becomes the recipient of the Holy Hours. This helps us to guard against an undue attachment to a specific priest. Each member commits to a Holy Hour on a specific day of the week, thus covering the entire week, every week. The commitment is to the assigned day; the Seven Sister may pray at any time on that day. If she is unable to offer her Holy Hour, she is to secure a substitute, explaining the Apostolate’s mission. The Holy Hour is ideally prayed in the presence of the Blessed Sacrament – either in an Adoration Chapel or in front of a Tabernacle – but not restricted to the parish of which the Seven Sister is a member. Thus, one can remain faithful to the commitment when traveling, when a parish does not offer Perpetual Adoration, or when there is limited access to a particular church. For more information or how to become part of the Apostolate, contact the Anchoress, Liz Gregorius, at [email protected] That Man is You What: "That Man is You!" program is an interactive, multimedia program designed for Catholic men, focusing on their roles as husbands, fathers, and leaders in society. TMIY is run by Paradius Dei, located in Houston, Texas. Paradisus Dei (Latin for "the Paradise of God") is a tax-exempt 501(c)3 organization founded in 2001 by Steve Bollman. Bollman, a former energy derivatives trader, founded the ministry in response to a call to renew marriage and family life. The organization's mission is to help families discover "the superabundance of God within marriage and family life". Paradisus Dei achieves this by producing "life-changing materials that expand the mind and touch the heart", integrating Church teachings with scientific findings and the wisdom of saints. The program is offered free to parishes and participants, with Paradisus Dei providing video series, manuals, training, and staff support. Currently there are over 1200 Catholic parishes involved in the TMIY program in both the U.S. and in 6 other countries. Each TMIY session is an interactive men's program combining the best research from science with the teachings of the Catholic faith and the wisdom of the saints to develop the vision of a Christian man fully alive. TMIY addresses modern pressures and temptations by integrating social and medical science with Catholic faith teachings and the wisdom of saints. It runs for 26 weeks, divided into Fall and Spring semesters. Meetings begin with breakfast & fellowship, followed by a TMIY video presentation, group discussion, and concluding with praying the Rosary together in the sanctuary. When: Every Saturday morning (except for Holiday weekends) at 6a.m. & finish at 7:30a.m. TMIY programs occur in sync with academic school years (i.e., Annual Program à Begins in Aug/Sep & Ends in Apr/May) Contact Klaus Sanford, [email protected] Women's Ministry/Walking with Purpose Walking With Purpose is part of a nationwide Catholic women’s ministry, that through their Bible Studies help women to know Jesus Christ personally by making Scripture and the teachings of the Catholic Church relevant and applicable. The program incorporates at-home Scripture study, weekly small group discussion, and monthly talks on relevant study material. Women of all ages are invited to join us Wednesday mornings, September through April, at Holy Spirit Parish Hall from 9-11am or from 6:30-8:00pm. Contact Judy Barranco, [email protected] , or Shonna Smith, [email protected] Walking with Purpose Calendar 8570 Vaughn Road, Montgomery, AL 36117Tel: 334-277-5631 Facebook Instagram Email Phone Login powered by eCatholic ®

Baptism Confirmation Holy Communion Reconciliation Anointing of the Sick Holy Matrimony Holy Orders Baptism The Sacrament of Baptism About the Sacrament of Baptism Baptism is necessary before one can receive any other sacrament. It is the first sacrament of Christian initiation which is completed with the sacraments of Confirmation and the Holy Eucharist. Baptism was instituted by Christ when he was baptized by St. John the Baptist and when he commanded his apostles to go and baptize all nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. (MT 28:19) Baptism removes all sins committed after birth and original sin. It makes us children of God, members of the Church, and heirs to the kingdom of heaven. Baptism imprints an indelible character on the soul of the recipient and can be received only once. Receiving the Sacrament The Sacrament of Baptism is regularly celebrated and can be administered both during Mass or outside of Mass. For adults, the Sacrament of Baptism is normally given after a period of preparation, usually through OCIA. Visit our OCIA page if you are an adult looking to be baptized in the Catholic Faith. If you would like to schedule a child or infant baptism, please contact Karen in the parish office. Parents are required to attend a baptism preparation class prior to scheduling a date for baptism. If a child is 8 years old or older, please contact Zavie George in Faith Formation. Additional classes for the child will be needed. Contact Karen, [email protected] , for more information. Choosing a Godparent These are the qualities needed for someone to serve as a godparent, or “sponsor”: Is a baptized Catholic who has received the Eucharist and has been Confirmed. Must be at least 16 years of age. Is a practicing Catholic who participates in the Eucharistic celebration on Sundays. Gives a good example of living their Catholic faith. Willing to encourage the child to develop and grow in the Catholic faith. If there are two sponsors, one must be male and the other female. The two godparents do not necessarily have to be of the same marriage. If they are living with someone like husband and wife, their marriage must be seen as valid in the eyes of the Catholic Church. A baptized non-Catholic may not be a sponsor but may serve as a Christian witness alongside a Catholic sponsor. Together they carry out the role of godparents in the baptism. Non-baptized persons may not serve in the role of sponsors or witnesses. Confirmation Confirmation Baptism, the Eucharist, and the sacrament of Confirmation together constitute the “sacraments of Christian initiation,” whose unity must be safeguarded. It must be explained to the faithful that the reception of the sacrament of Confirmation is necessary for the completion of baptismal grace. For “by the sacrament of Confirmation, [the baptized] are more perfectly bound to the Church and are enriched with a special strength of the Holy Spirit. Hence they are, as true witnesses of Christ, more strictly obliged to spread and defend the faith by word and deed.” Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1285 Youth in the 11th grade or higher are eligible to prepare for the sacrament of Confirmation. The preparation includes the children participating in Confirmation classes, retreats, and service projects, interviews and rehearsals. A copy of the child’s Baptismal certificate is required. The Archbishop will determine the date. Contact Sarah Rose Burden for more information, [email protected] Holy Communion Holy Communion The holy Eucharist completes Christian initiation. Those who have been raised to the dignity of the royal priesthood by Baptism and configured more deeply to Christ by Confirmation participate with the whole community in the Lord’s own sacrifice by means of the Eucharist. “At the Last Supper, on the night he was betrayed, our Savior instituted the Eucharistic sacrifice of his Body and Blood. This he did in order to perpetuate the sacrifice of the cross throughout the ages until he should come again, and so to entrust to his beloved Spouse, the Church, a memorial of his death and resurrection: a sacrament of love, a sign of unity, a bond of charity, a Paschal banquet ‘in which Christ is consumed, the mind is filled with grace, and a pledge of future glory is given to us.'” Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1322-23 The celebration of these sacraments are very special faith experiences in our parish. Children in the 2nd grade are eligible to prepare for the sacraments of First Reconciliation and First Eucharist. A copy of the child’s Baptismal certificate is required. Contact Zavie George for more information, [email protected] Reconciliation Reconciliation Those who approach the sacrament of Penance obtain pardon from God’s mercy for the offense committed against him, and are, at the same time, reconciled with the Church which they have wounded by their sins and which by charity, by example, and by prayer labors for their conversion. Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1422 See Confession Times here. Anointing of the Sick Anointing of the Sick “By the sacred anointing of the sick and the prayer of the priests the whole Church commends those who are ill to the suffering and glorified Lord, that he may raise them up and save them. And indeed she exhorts them to contribute to the good of the People of God by freely uniting themselves to the Passion and death of Christ.” Catechism of the Catholic Church, 1499 Contact the parish office or priest when a family member is ill or in the hospital. For a hospital stay that is scheduled, please call to request a celebration of the Sacrament of Anointing of the Sick. Contact the Parish Office, 334-277-5631 Holy Matrimony Holy Matrimony About this Sacrament The Sacrament of Marriage is a covenant between a husband and wife. This covenant is a permanent union of persons capable of knowing and loving each other and God. In the bond of Matrimony, husbands and wives give themselves totally and selflessly to one another for life: they are to love one another as Christ loves the Church. Any couple, one man and one woman, who are baptized and are free to marry may receive this sacrament. This means that the man and woman wishing to marry each other must meet the age requirements and any other requirements established by civil and church law. The grace of this Sacrament perfects the love of husband and wife, binds them together in fidelity, and helps them welcome and care for children. Christ is the source of this grace and he dwells with the spouses to strengthen their covenant promises, to bear each other's burdens with forgiveness and kindness, and to experience ahead of time the "wedding feast of the Lamb" (Rev 19:9). Receiving the Sacrament Couples planning to be married should notify the parish office at least six months in advance of their wedding date. This will ensure adequate time to make arrangements and to complete the required sacramental marriage preparation program. Contact the Parish Office for more information, 334-277-5631 or [email protected] . Holy Orders Holy Orders About this Sacrament "[Jesus] calls [us] individually by name. Each one of us — clergy, religious, layperson, married, single, adult, child — has a personal vocation. God intends each one of us to play a unique role in carrying out the divine plan." U.S. Catholic Catechism for Adults, pg. 452. Men and women may be called to the religious life, single life, or married life. The sacrament of Holy Orders was instituted by Christ at the Last Supper. The grace of the sacrament imprints an indelible character on the soul of the recipient and configures him to Christ. Only baptized men may receive the sacrament of Orders and only once in each of its degrees: deacon, priest, and bishop. Only men willing to embrace celibacy may be ordained as bishops and priests. Unmarried men may be ordained as deacons if they embrace celibacy. Married men may be ordained as deacons if they are willing never to marry again (even if a spouse should die). The practice of ordaining only baptized men rests on the decision of Christ to call only men to these orders in the Church. Not even Mary, the Immaculate Conception, was called by Christ to be a deacon, priest, or bishop. Please reach out to Fr. Connor Plessala ( [email protected] ), the Archdiocesan Vocation Director to learn more information about ordained ministry or the religious life (communities for men and women). Also please reach out to our Pastor, particularly on the many ways you can be involved in our parish as you continue discerning. What is ACYC? ACYC stands for the Archdiocesan Catholic Youth Conference , an annual Catholic youth conference hosted by the Archdiocese of Mobile . ACYC brings Catholic teenagers from parishes throughout the Archdiocese together for an unforgettable experience centered on Jesus Christ, the Catholic faith, friendship, and community . Over the course of the conference, young people have the opportunity to step outside of their everyday routines and experience the Catholic Church in a whole new way. ACYC combines powerful talks, music and worship, prayer, the Sacraments, small-group discussions, fellowship, activities, and plenty of fun to create an environment where teens can encounter Christ and grow in their faith. But ACYC is about more than a weekend away. A Church Bigger Than Your Parish For many teens, ACYC is the first time they experience just how many young Catholics are part of the Church in our area. Students come together from parishes across the Archdiocese of Mobile, giving them the opportunity to make new friends, share their faith, and discover that they are part of something much bigger than their own parish community. ACYC seeks to foster unity among our parishes and energize young people in their Catholic faith , encouraging them to grow deeper in their relationship with Jesus Christ and His Church. A Place to Encounter Christ ACYC creates space for young people to pray, ask questions, learn, worship, laugh, make friendships, and encounter Jesus in a personal and meaningful way. Whether a teen is deeply involved in their faith, still figuring out what they believe, or simply looking for a place to belong, ACYC welcomes them. The goal is not simply to give young people a fun weekend, but to help them encounter Christ, strengthen their faith, and return home ready to live that faith in their everyday lives. At Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos, we are excited to give our teens the opportunity to be part of this incredible Catholic community and experience the joy of being young and Catholic together. How do I get it? What Can I Do With Hallow? Frequently Asked Questions What is Hallow? It’s Not "Just Another App…" We Spend So Much Time on Our Phones… Our phones have become such a big part of our everyday lives. We use them to work, communicate, scroll, shop, keep up with the news, take pictures, and fill the little quiet moments throughout our day. So why not use them for something good? Why not take the device we already carry with us everywhere and use it to spend a few minutes with the One who gave everything to save us? Hallow gives us a simple way to turn those everyday moments into opportunities for prayer. Instead of reaching for your phone only to scroll, you can reach for it to pray the Rosary. Instead of filling a quiet moment with noise, you can spend it with Scripture. Instead of ending the day scrolling, you can end it in prayer. It doesn’t have to be complicated. It doesn’t have to take an hour. Sometimes, a few intentional minutes with God can change the way we carry the rest of our day. Our phones can certainly be a distraction from our faith, but they can also become a tool that helps us grow in it. What if we used the technology we already have to draw us closer to Christ? That’s what Hallow is here to help us do. ❤️ How do I get it? Getting Started with Hallow Getting started with Hallow is simple! The app is available for both Apple and Android devices. Phones, Tablets, and you can even access it on the web! (For best experience, mobile version is recommended. Not all features are accessible on web version.) 1. Download the Hallow App Search for Hallow in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store and download the app to your phone. 2. Create Your Account Open the app and follow the prompts to create your Hallow account. You’ll be able to personalize your experience based on your prayer life and the areas where you’d like to grow. 3. Connect with Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos Parish Once your account is created, search for Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos Parish within Hallow and connect with our parish community. 4. Start Praying! Explore the different prayer options and find something that fits naturally into your day. Start with five minutes if that’s all you have. There’s no need to make it complicated. Already have Hallow? You don’t need to create a new account. Simply log in to your existing Hallow account and look for Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos Parish to connect with our parish community. ​ Download for iPhone or iPad ​​​​ Download for Android ​​​ What Can I Do With Hallow? So Much More Than Meditation.. Hallow gives you access to thousands of guided prayer experiences designed to help you make prayer a regular part of your everyday life. Whether you have 5 minutes or 30 , there are ways to pray that can fit naturally into your day. Pray the Rosary Pray along with guided Rosaries and spend time meditating on the mysteries of Christ. Pray with Scripture Spend time with God’s Word through Scripture meditation, Lectio Divina, and Gospel reflections. ✝️ Grow in Catholic Prayer Explore traditional Catholic prayers, litanies, novenas, the Examen, Morning Prayer, Night Prayer, and more. ️ Spend Time in Stillness Slow down, quiet the noise around you, and simply make space to be present with God. ❤️ Pray Through Every Season Hallow offers prayer experiences for Advent, Christmas, Lent, Easter, feast days, difficult seasons, special intentions, and more. ⛪ Pray Together as a Parish Hallow gives us the opportunity to pray not only on our own, but together as a parish family. Through BFXS, you’ll be able to participate in prayer challenges with other members of our parish , creating opportunities for us to build a stronger and more intentional prayer life together. These prayer challenges are hand-selected by Father Jim Cink with our parish community in mind. They give us a simple way to pray together, even when we aren’t physically together. Imagine knowing that while you’re praying in your car, at home, on your lunch break, or before bed, other members of our BFXS family are praying right alongside you. Connect With Your BFXS Community Prayer is one way we grow together, but faith is meant to be lived in community, too. Through Hallow, you can also connect with BFXS small groups and ministry communities. Our parish has many opportunities to find people who share your interests, your stage of life, or simply your desire to grow closer to Christ. Some of our groups include: Men of Saint Joseph Women’s Bible Study EPIC High School Welcome Home Catholic ✝️ OCIA …and many more! Whether you’re looking for Scripture study, fellowship, faith formation, a place to ask questions, or simply people to walk alongside you, there is a place for you. We don’t have to pray alone. We can encourage one another, challenge one another, and grow together in our relationship with Christ. ❤️ You Don’t Have to Know Exactly What to Pray. You just have to be willing to begin. Hallow gives you a place to start. And through BFXS, we can pray together. Frequently Asked Questions Frequently Asked Questions What is Hallow? Hallow is a Catholic prayer and meditation app designed to help you develop a deeper and more consistent prayer life. It offers guided prayer experiences including the Rosary, Scripture meditation, daily Gospel reflections, novenas, litanies, the Examen, and more. Do I have to be Catholic to use Hallow? No. Hallow is designed to be accessible to anyone who wants to spend time in prayer and grow closer to God. While many of its resources are rooted in Catholic tradition, you do not have to be Catholic to use the app. Is Hallow free? Hallow offers some content at no cost, while a subscription provides access to the full library of prayer content and additional features. As part of our partnership with Hallow, all parish members will receive 50% off paid subscriptions through 2028. Additionally, we are offering a limited number of complimentary one-year subscriptions to parishioners through our prayer subscription scholarship request process. How do I connect with Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos Parish? After creating your Hallow account, search for Blessed Francis Xavier Seelos Parish within the app and follow the prompts to connect with our parish community. What are the BFXS prayer challenges? Throughout the year, Father Jim Cink will hand-select prayer challenges for our parish community. These give us an opportunity to pray together and build stronger prayer habits, even when we’re not physically together. Do I have to participate in the parish prayer challenges? No. They’re completely optional. They’re simply an opportunity for anyone who would like to join other members of our parish in prayer. I already have a Hallow account. Can I still connect with BFXS? Yes! You can use your existing Hallow account. You do not need to create a new account simply to connect with our parish. How do I request a complimentary one-year subscription? Visit our Hallow Prayer Subscription Request page and complete the Google Form. Requests will be prayerfully reviewed by Father Jim Cink . Because the number of subscriptions is limited, submitting a request does not guarantee that a subscription will be awarded. What if I don’t know how to pray? That’s okay. ❤️ You don’t need to be an experienced prayer to begin using Hallow. The guided prayers are designed to help you simply press play, slow down, and spend time with God. Do I have to spend a lot of time praying? Not at all. Hallow has prayer experiences of different lengths, including short prayers that can fit into even the busiest day. Start with what you can give. Even a few intentional minutes can be a beautiful way to turn your heart toward God. Is Hallow a replacement for Mass or the Sacraments? No. Hallow is a tool to support your personal prayer life . It doesn’t replace Mass, the Sacraments, Scripture, or the life of the Church. Think of it as a resource that can help you carry your prayer life into the rest of your week. Still Have Questions? If you have a question about Hallow or need help getting connected with BFXS, please contact the Theresa at the Parish Office or Jalyse Schwahl . We’re happy to help you get started. ACYC Facebook Phone Email Search Search Home About About Us Join Our Parish Our Patron Saint Bulletins Who We Are Contact Us Resources Parish Forms Sacramental Life Mass Times Liturgy Resources Homilies & Worship Aides Parish Life Altar Servers Greeters Ushers Lectors Eucharistic Ministers Faith Formation Religious Education Youth Group Confirmation Events & News Calendar Photo Albums Give Online Giving Building Campaign Stewardship Time & Talent Treasure BFXS + Hallow Our Patron Saint Francis Xavier Seelos was born on January 11, 1819 in Fussen, Bavaria, Germany. He was baptized on the same day in the parish church of St. Mang. Having expressed a desire for the priesthood since childhood, he entered the diocesan seminary in 1842 after having completed his studies in philosophy. Soon after meeting the missionaries of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer (Redemptorists), founded for the evangelization of the most abandoned, he decided to enter the Congregation and to minister to the German speaking immigrants in the United States. He was accepted by the Congregation on November 22, 1842, and sailed the following year from Le Havre, France arriving in New York on April 20, 1843. On December 22, 1844, after having completed his novitiate and theological studies, Seelos was ordained a priest in the Redemptorist Church of St. James in Baltimore, Maryland, U.S.A. The Men of St. Joseph What is The Men St. Jospeh? "The Men of St. Joseph is an association of Christian men, united under the Catholic Church, who meet weekly to pray together and encourage each other to be the spiritual leaders of their families. The purpose of the Men of St. Joseph is to instill holiness in men and facilitate spiritual leadership in family and community life." What a different world it would be if more men dedicated themselves to holiness and embraced their role as their family’s spiritual leader. What if your parish and community was full of men like this? We ask our men to help “put the family in the hands of the Father”. By this we mean the desire for men to lead by example and through that example help place himself, his family, his friends, and community into the hands of our Heavenly Father. In short, help lead those around him to holiness. Weekly meetings which consist of prayer, reading about the ultimate example of holy manliness in our Lord Jesus in the Gospel, and a discussion of the practical application of that example in today’s world. This weekly prescription help give men the tools, confidence, and support of other men, to become the spiritual leaders we are all called to be. Our hope, is that participation in the Men of St. Joseph meetings will lead to invigorated spiritual lives of Catholic men, and by their positive influence, to that of our families, friends and co-workers. Why should I join? As a man you have a deep, almost instinctual call to accomplish and have impact. That need is what drives men to discover new worlds, develop new technologies, and accomplish “impossible tasks”. It’s also with pushes us to succeed in business, build, create, hunt, fish, and compete in sports. But in the end we are all called for more than reaching the mountain tops of this world. Our ultimate goal is much more significant: Eternal Life with Christ. For most of us that can seem more daunting than scaling a high cliff face. But the truth is that is what men are built to do. Men are called to be spiritual leaders. Our number one goal in life is not wealth or professional esteem but to get ourselves, our wives, children, and even our friends to heaven. It may seem an impossible task but it’s not. Our calling to become spiritual leaders becomes easier when we have the accountability, support, and example of other men all focused on the same goal. That is the purpose of the Men of St. Joseph. And that is why we hope you will join us. The Men of St Joseph is designed to give you the structure, insight, confidence and support you need to help get you and your family to heaven. In the end we have to ask ourselves, is there anything more important than that? Join the Men of St. Joseph. Help yourself and your family climb that Most Important Mountain. What are the meetings like? The hour-long meetings are simple. The meetings begin with group prayers from the Magnificat*, followed by prayer intentions, then a reading from the Gospel or an apologetic text, and finally discussion. Simply put: read, pray and discuss. Men of St. Joseph is not a “small-group” organization. It is common to start a group with 5 or 6 men, but depending on parish size, chapters grow to 20, 30, 40, or more men. Growth is encouraged. During the discussion portion of meetings, though, some of the larger groups do break out into smaller groups, to facilitate discussion. Holy Days of Obligation The Church imposes on us the Obligation to attend and participate in Sunday Mass and Mass on Holy Days of Obligation. They both carry the same weight, or obligation. Holy Days of Obligation are Solemnities that celebrate particular mysteries of the Faith that are recognized to be so important that they necessitate our presence at Mass. Holiday Mass Times Christmas Mass Times Saturday, December 24th 5:00pm Our Lady of Bon Secour Midnight Mass Sunday, December 25th 12:00am St John the Baptist Thursday, December 8th 9:00am St John the Baptist New Years Eve / Day Masses Saturday, December 31 5:00pm Our Lady of Bon Secour Saturday December 31 11:00pm Adoration and Holy Hour of the Holy Spirit St John the Baptist Midnight Mass Sunday, January 1, 2023 12:00am St John the Baptist Sunday, January 1, 2023 9:00am St John the Baptist January 1, 2023 11:00am Our Lady of Bon Secour Complete List of Holy Days of Obligation: January 1 - The solemnity of Mary, Mother of God August 15 - The solemnity of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary November 1 - The solemnity of All Saints December 8 - The solemnity of the Immaculate Conception December 25 - The solemnity of the Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ If January 1, August 15, or November 1 fall on a Saturday or on a Monday, the obligation for Mass attendance is lifted. However, when December 8, or December 25 fall on a Saturday or a Monday, the obligation for Mass remains. Further, the Sunday obligation for Mass also remains and you are Obligated to attend Mass for BOTH the Solemnity and the Sunday. *please note, in the Archdiocese of Mobile, the Solemnity of the Ascension is moved to the Seventh Sunday of Easter, elsewhere this Solemnity may remain on Thursday of the Sixth Week of Easter, where is remains a Holy Day of Obligation. 10800 St Johns Ln, Foley, AL 36535 (251) 965-7719 Ministries & Sacraments RCIA Men of St Joseph St Anne Guild Religious Education Reconciliation St John the Baptist Contact Join the Parish Mass Times Finance Pray with Us! We are grateful for all that the Sodality has done for our Church throughout the years and are excited to see this organization to grow, mature, and blossom into something even greater. There are three pillars on which the Saint Ann Guild will stand: Spiritual Motherhood, Communion of Catholic Women, and the Financial Care of our Parish and surrounding community. Spiritual Motherhood Prayer is the most needed thing in our Parish. The role of the guild in this regard will be unpacked at the Lenten Women's Retreat Day on March 20, 12:00-4:00PM. Sign up for our e-newsletters and emails by clicking HERE . You can also follow us on Instagram and Facebook for pictures and other updates. We do not communicate exclusively with students; all communication is public via social media or communications with parents. Archdiocese of Mobile Office of Youth Ministry Archdiocese of Mobile Office of Religious Education Our Ministry Philosophy EDGE is a Catholic middle school youth ministry program that provides a safe, fun place for youth to find a solid Catholic community, to get answers to their questions about faith, and most importantly, to experience Jesus in a profound and personal way. EDGE speaks to the physical, psychological, cognitive, relational, and spiritual maturation of middle school youth. We aim to provide resources and curriculum that present Catholic teaching in a way that young people can understand. THE ALLEY - CTK's Youth House The Alley is the Christ the King Youth Ministry House. Located on 810 Trione Ave, The Alley provides a home away from home environment where teens can relax, enjoy fellowship with one another, grow in faith, and participate in faith formation, games, and more. Located behind The Alley is the CTK Athletic Complex that is often used for Life Teen/EDGE events and sporting games. The Alley was renovated in Spring 2017 providing a new space for seating, games, and more. Join us on Sunday nights or at many additional events at The Alley. In case you were curious, The Alley is named after St. Aloysius Gonzaga, patron saint of Catholic Youth! Edge Policies Only students in grade 6-8 are allowed to attend EDGE activities. Younger or older siblings/relatives are not allowed to attend unless prior permission is granted. During the summer, rising 7-9 th graders may participate in EDGE activities. Rising 6 th graders will be welcomed in the fall. EDGE Code of Conduct EDGE Students will: respect themselves, other people, other people’s property, and the church property. be encouragers, not one who ridicules, makes fun of, or criticizes. respect and maintain the privacy of information shared at the group activities. peacefully with anger and disagreements. participate and contribute in a positive way in all group activities and obey the instructions of the Youth Ministry staff and volunteers. show respect by not causing disruptions and not talking unless called on to respond. use language that reflects a Christian attitude and will not use curse words or other foul language. keep my hands to myself: no tickling, wrestling, or inappropriate touching. Physical displays of affection such as kissing, full body hugs, sitting on laps, and lying or sleeping next to each other are inappropriate; being isolated or alone with another student is not allowed. wear modest clothing because we are temples of the Holy Spirit. T-shirts or other clothing with suggestive, degrading, evil, vulgar, illegal, or inappropriate content will not be permitted. not use cell phones, iPods, cameras or other personal electronic or entertainment devices during activities and services. (special rules apply to trips) stay with the group at all times. For example, if we are having a meeting in the Youth Center, students will not leave the Youth Center. If we are on a trip, students will stay with the group. not leave any activity, service, or trip before its published ending time without approval from a parent or guardian “in person” or by phone. not possess a gun, long blade knife, or any other weapon at any Youth Ministry activity. not use, possess or be under the influence of alcohol, tobacco, marijuana or other illegal drugs at any Youth Ministry activity. not engage in sexual intimacy or sexual harassment, and will not possess pornography at any Youth Ministry activity. EDGE students promise to behave in a way becoming a young Christian adult and to follow directions and rules, knowing that they represent our parish family and the Archdiocese of Mobile. If they do not follow these standards, they understand they can be dismissed from the trip at their parent/guardian’s expense. In years past, it was most commonly administered to the dying for the remission of sins and the provision of spiritual strength and health. In modern times, however, its use has been expanded to all who are gravely ill or are about to undergo a serious operation. This sacrament of healing provides strengthening of the soul and often of the body as well. As with the sacraments of Reconciliation and Eucharist, it can be repeated as often as is necessary. It is our duty to provide a Christ-centered atmosphere for all of our participants. Bathing suits for guys and girls should be modest. If you have any question about whether it is modest enough, you should not bring it. Girls must wear a modest one-piece bathing suit with shorts over it. Bikinis and triangle tops are not allowed—girl’s bathing suits cannot make any kind of “v” in the chest. Bathing suits should have no cutouts where skin is showing. If you do not have a bathing suit that fits into these criteria, you can wear a colored t-shirt over it and shorts over your own bathing suit. Be prepared for our chaperones to ask you to wear a t-shirt or shorts over your bathing suit if they agree it is not appropriate. Boys’ boxers should not be seen under too short bathing suits (or shorts). They travel from Mobile, Stockton, Spanish Fort, Daphne, Montrose, Fairhope, Point Clear, Robertsdale, Loxley, Magnolia Springs, Foley and Gulf Shores. Some are even Episcopalian, Anglican and Lutheran. For five years, over 430 committed, weekly guardians of the Blessed Sacrament have created a powerhouse of prayer by adoring Jesus at Christ the King’s Blessed Sacrament Chapel in Daphne. This beautiful outpouring of faith and love has enabled everyone the opportunity to visit Jesus anytime during the day or night on the Eastern Shore. Drop-in visits number over 1000 a week, thanks to a diligent committee of 30 men and women who work to insure all 168 weekly hours are covered with faithful prayer guardians always before the Blessed Sacrament. Mother Teresa and John Paul II were living examples of the fruits of Eucharistic Adoration. No matter how busy they were or how many important people they had to see, they made sure that they spent time with the most important Person of all: Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Every day they spent 2 to 3 hours in His Eucharistic Presence, and they told the whole world that this was where they got all their energy to do so much for God and His people. If you feel called to grow closer to Jesus and show your love to Him in a radical way, consider committing one hour a week with Him. For more information visit ctkdaphne.org or call Missy Schmidt at 251-626-7427. Click here to watch the anniversary video A five year celebration of PEA was held March 12th with a mass, dinner, and video presentation. Father Paul Zoghby was guest celebrant and speaker with over 250 in attendance. Christ the King’s Blessed Sacrament Chapel is the only perpetual adoration chapel south of Montgomery, AL and east of New Orleans, LA. “The Church and the world have a great need for Eucharistic worship. Jesus awaits us in this Sacrament of Love. Let us not refuse the time to go to meet Him in Adoration, in contemplation full of faith, and open to making amends for the serious offenses and crimes of the world. Let our Adoration never cease.” Saint Pope John Paul II Why go to Adoration? You go to Adoration to deepen your personal relationship with Jesus and grow in faith, hope, and love. Jesus will give you His peace within you as you spend time with Him. Just as you can’t be exposed to the sun without receiving its rays, neither can you come into the light and presence of Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament without receiving the divine rays of His grace, His love and His peace. What do I do during my hour? You may spend the time with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament any way you want. You may read the Bible, write in a prayer journal, bring spiritual books (or read some from our library), pray the rosary, or just sit, relax and enjoy the peace that comes from being in His Presence. You may feel you can’t pray well. Don’t let that discourage you. The fact that you come to spend time with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament pleases Him very much and is, in itself, a prayer of faith. How can I show my Love for Jesus? You can show your love by making a weekly commitment to Him. By kneeling on both knees before going into the pews, you acknowledge His True Presence. As you lift your mind and heart to Jesus during Adoration, try thinking about His suffering and believe He suffered all He did because you are very precious and worth everything to Him! “Our essential commitment in life is to grow spiritually in the climate of the Holy Eucharist.” Saint Pope John Paul II Parish Office Mailing Address 711 College Avenue Daphne, AL 36526 tel: (251) 626-2343 fax: (251) 621-1640 Map Church 1505 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Parish Library 1702 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Assumption Hall 1501 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Rectory 715 College Avenue Daphne, AL 36526 Map Immaculata Center 1601 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Blessed Sacrament Chapel 1505-A Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map The Alley 810 Trione Avenue Daphne, AL 36526 tel: (251) 626-3992 Map Copyright © Christ the King Catholic Church Login powered by eCatholic ®

Nikki Kingsley September 12 6:30 pm in the church Welcome What is the Truth? This was the burning question that led Nikki Kingsley on her journey from Islam to Christianity. Nikki’s remarkable story began in Pakistan where she was born in a Muslim family. She arrived in America at the age of thirty with her two young children, seeking freedom from an arranged marriage, and discovered the promise found in the dream called America. Nikki’s life went through a dramatic turn when she had an extraordinary series of mystical experiences. These events prompted her to question and reconsider the Muslim faith that she had practiced for 40 years. Ultimately, this led Nikki to The Truth in the person of Jesus Christ. A compelling speaker, Nikki now shares her life-changing story of faith and hope––a story of a journey from the culture, faith, and traditions of the East to the freedom of the West. She has been a guest on many Catholic shows including The Journey Home on EWTN, Ave Maria Radio, The Catholic Channel on Sirius XM, and a speaker at many Catholic conferences and retreats. Nikki Kingsley’s dynamic account of her faith journey from darkness into Light is detailed in her book, Thirst for Truth: From Mohammad to Jesus, and can be purchased on her website at nikkikingsley.com. Click HERE to for registration information. Basketball is open to all students enrolled in CTK Faith Formation or CTKCS in 1st - 8th grades. The addition of 1st graders is new this year, and we are excited to include our 1st graders in the basketball program! The girls uniforms are different this year. The 1st - 4th grade girls will continue to wear the dry-fit T-shirt type jerseys that are currently used for soccer. So, if you have one of those, no need to order a new jersey. These girls can wear any navy blue shorts, most wear Nike/Under Armour type. The 5th - 8th grade girls are wearing true basketball uniforms. These are the sleeveless jerseys currently being worn by our volleyball teams. If your daughter is playing volleyball right now, all you will need are the shorts. If you are not currently playing volleyball, you will need to order a full uniform for any girls in grades 5th - 8th. The boys in all divisions will continue to wear the same uniforms. The deadline to register is Tuesday October 30. There will be no registrations allowed after October 30. All fees must be paid by October 30 to have a jersey ordered or have your child added to a roster. Start dates for practice will be scheduled soon. In the meantime, get your registration done today! Thank you and Go Saints! Its purpose was to establish permanent scholarships for the education of men for the priesthood from the Archdiocese of Mobile. We collect funds throughout the year, but especially on BURSE Sunday, which is September 10. We present these funds to the Archbishop at the Annual ACCW Convention in the fall. These monies are then invested and used for the education of our seminarians. In 1953, the dues were set at $12.00 annually and have not been raised in 64 years. Membership is open to everyone! There are no meetings to attend; no committees to serve on; just your prayers for vocations and your financial support. Please join the Priests Burse Club to help our 14 seminarians studying for the priesthood. Chris Stewart is the co-founder of Casting Nets Ministries. He has served as youth minister, junior high religion teacher, as well as high school and college theology professor. Chris and his lovely wife, Maria, live in Wichita, KS with their seven children. Hector Molina is the CEO of Casting Nets Ministries. He is a former apologist for Catholic Answers and past Director of Evangelization for the Archdiocese of St. Louis. Hector and his lovely wife, Uki, live in St. Louis, MO with their six children.
