We will reassess the situation late this year to determine if classes will resume in the new year. The parish First Holy Communion which would have taken place in May has been rescheduled for Sunday, September 27 at 2:00pm. Additional information will be sent to the families of last year’s 2nd Grade students. In an effort to continue rising 2nd Grade students on their sacramental journey, 2020-2021 sacramental preparation for First Reconciliation and First Holy Communion will be offered. Additional information will be sent to the families of last year’s 1st Grade students. New families and/or new students who will be entering 2nd - 8th and have NOT received these sacraments should contact our Director of Religious Education, Sam Di Benedetto, at [email protected] or by calling our Parish Office at 251-626-2343 by October 16. Tracking Mary: Mysteries & Messages Welcome Tracking Mary: Mysteries & Messages Get your Golden Ticket To "Track" Mary All Over The World! First stop, France, then FULL STEAM AHEAD to Portugal, Mexico, Ireland & England. The Queen of Heaven Express is Leaving the Station! Discover how Mary brings us closer to Jesus through the POWER of the Rosary. Mysteries and Messages are revealed at each stop. Experience the wonder of Our Lady of Lourdes, Our Lady of Fatima, Our Lady of Guadalupe, Our Lady of Knock and Our Lady of Mount Carmel. This exciting adventure offers Union Station Skits, Full Steam Faith, Boxcar Bible, Gondola Games, Caboose Crafts, Stoker Snacks & Steam Whistle Music! Click here to download the registration form. This decision was made after much careful thought, prayer, and discussion. Our focus is on the health and safety of our children as they return to the classroom next week. Our school administrators and staff have worked extremely hard to prepare for a smooth and successful reopening. Although we are all extremely disappointed for our athletes and families, we know that CYO Sports will return stronger and better than ever before. A modified Toy Bowl is being discussed and we will have more information soon in regards to this annual 8th grade tradition. May God bless you and your families and keep you all safe and healthy. Its six short chapters contain some of the most discussed passages in the New Testament. This 4-session study examines many important themes that are still relevant in today’s Christian culture and society—the nature of marriage, the purpose and role of the Church, the preeminence of grace in God’s plan, and the reality of spiritual warfare. Email Steve Coppejans at [email protected] to register. Through the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, Dominican Friars have been proclaiming the truth of God's Word for over 800 years in order to bring Catholics into a personal encounter with the Living Christ Who reveals the unconditional love of our heavenly Father. The iMercy missiom is a unique, grace-filled evangelical moment in the life of a parish led by the Dominican Friars. This mission aims to help parishioners enter more deeply into the love of the Holy Trinity and experience God's merciful touch through the Sacraments. Officers for 2017-18 are Cheryl Miller (President), Lisa Boos (Vice President), Carol Palumbo (Secretary), Diane Sublett (Treasurer), and Sandra Hrabovsky (Member at Large). The MOSJ Outback retreat is designed for two persons to attend together, thus our retreat was composed of mothers and fathers attending with their teen sons and daughters as "campers". The campers experienced several reflective talks and outdoor activities that included a challenging high-ropes course, all designed to build, restore, and strengthen relationships with each other and with God. In order to facilitate this event, a volunteer team was formed made up of over one-hundred lay persons, largely from CTK and St. Lawrence parishes, and integrated with MOSJ volunteers from Mobile. Fr. Victor of Christ the King Parish led the campers through celebrations of the Mass and adoration, and confessions were heard with the help of six assisting priests. The Holy Spirit clearly had a large impact on both the campers and volunteers during the weekend, and it is hoped that the MOSJ Outback retreat will continue as part of our Confirmation program, with both the support of all involved, as well as those called to assist with this great event in the future. This retreat, the first ever MOSJ Outback retreat used by an entire parish as a jumpstarter for Confirmation formation, was made possible by the extreme support and generosity of the MOSJ. An experience which normally costs a parent/teen couple $295 was offered to our parishioners for only $25 a couple! Moving forward, we need your support to be able to offer this program to next year's Confirmation class and hopefully many classes to come. Consider making a donation to support this bold new ministry in our parish family by going to the following link: http://www.menofstjoseph.com , clicking "Donate Now" and marking "MOSJ Outback" before finalizing payment. Having had the MOSJ invest in our parish in such a big way, it's now our chance to "pay it forward" and keep costs low so everyone in our parish can benefit from such a dynamic, faith building experience. Dear Brothers and Sisters in the Lord, I am Thomas J. Rodi, the Archbishop of Mobile and I welcome you to take part in a Novena for the Healing of our Hearts and Home. I welcome in a special way all Catholics, Christians of other denominations and people of good will who are reading this and who live throughout the southern 28 counties of Alabama which comprise the Archdiocese of Mobile, our common home. I pray that this may be a powerful way in which we can join together as brothers and sisters, perhaps as never before, to humble ourselves before our God asking him to pour out his mercy and grace upon us to heal our hearts and home—that is, to use this trying time to draw us closer to God and to deliver us from this tragic pandemic. The term “novena” comes from the Latin word “novem” meaning “nine” and is the traditional term Catholics use for a prayer that is offered for a special intention for nine successive days. Why 9 days? Because after Jesus ascended into heaven, Mary and the apostles gathered together for nine days to pray for and await the coming of the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:3-14). Ever since the early Church received the Holy Spirit, it has been a tradition to implore God for nine consecutive days with a petition of great importance.* Tragedies, like the one we are facing, have a way of getting our attention and potentially drawing us closer to God. However this is not automatic. We have to allow ourselves to be humbled by the circumstances of life, renew our trust in God and invite him to change us for the better. Otherwise, the same tragedies may easily make us cynical and bitter leading us to resent God if not to reject him completely. Consequently, as your brother in the Lord I feel compelled to lead all of us in humbling ourselves before the only one who can completely heal our hearts and our common home—God. We just celebrated Easter, God’s triumph over sin and death. Let us not be afraid to take this unique time as an opportunity to call upon the mercy and grace of God to triumph over this pandemic and all that threatens to draw us apart from God. Let us ask him to take this cross we bear and transform it with his mercy into the peace and joy of the Resurrection. Let us pray that God may newly pour out his peace and joy over the all the world and in a particular way over all of us here in the southern half of Alabama. I have chosen to lead you in two prayers during this Novena. One is the Chaplet of Divine Mercy. It is a prayer which Jesus himself taught to St. Faustina and asked her to spread around the world. One central prayer repeats throughout the chaplet—“For the sake of his sorrowful passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world.” This is exactly what we need God to do during this time—“have mercy on us and the whole world.” The other prayer is a “Litany of Repentance” which highlights some of the ways that we have strayed from God. I have no idea why God is allowing this pandemic to affect our world. However, I do know it is an opportunity for us to slow down, realize what really matters in life and turn towards God with new fervor. So let us kneel down together ask God to heal our Hearts and our Home, so that both may be filled with the peace and joy of the Risen Lord! Sincerely in Christ, Thomas J. Rodi Archbishop of Mobile *The name of the day “Pentecost” itself is derived from the Greek word "pentecoste," meaning 50th. This is the Greek translation for the Jewish holiday, Shavu`ot, which falls 50 days after Passover. Shavu’ot is sometimes called the “Festival of Weeks,” referring to the seven weeks since Passover. Originally a harvest feast, Shavu`ot now commemorates the sealing of the Old Covenant on Mount Sinai, when the Lord revealed the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai. Every year, the Jewish people renew their acceptance of the gift of the Torah on this feast. The Resurrection occurred on the Feast of First Fruits. Pentecost (Shavu’ot) was seven weeks later. Again that’s why it’s sometimes called the “Feast of Weeks.” However, the actual dates of both were established by counting from the first Sabbath after Passover (also the day Jesus died on the Cross—Good Friday). First Fruits was the first day after the Sabbath (the first after Passover) and Pentecost was the 50th day, so there were only 49 days between First Fruits (Jesus’ Ressurection—Easter Sunday) and Pentecost. Acts 1:3 says that Jesus ascended into Heaven 40 days after His Resurrection (41 days after the Sabbath). That means Pentecost was 9 days later, not 10. In Scripture, the number 9 often marks the end, or conclusion of a matter. The arrival of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost marked the end of the Lord’s personal ministry on Earth and the beginning of his work through the Holy Spirit in his body the Church. Whereas “Pentecost” once celebrated the acceptance of God’s written law contained in the Torah, it now celebrates when God poured our his Holy Spirit upon the Church, writing his law upon our hearts. (Jer 31:33, Ez 11:19-20, Heb 10:16) In John 16:7 the Lord had told His Disciples, “I tell you the truth: It is for your good that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Counselor will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. February 2 Welcome FAITH FORMATION Two Sessions Each Day Monday, January 30 9:00 AM : Morning Mass & Mission Talk 6:30 PM: Mission Talk & Sacrament of Reconciliation Tuesday, January 31 - Wednesday, February 1 9:00 AM : Morning Mass & Mission Talk 6:30 PM: Mass & Mission Talk Thursday, February 2 9:00 AM : Morning Mass & Mission Talk 6:30 PM: Mass, Mission Talk, & Eucharistic Healing Service Themes Monday – Reconciliation [Confessions will be heard] Tuesday– The Priesthood & The Eucharist Wednesday – The Lord, The Giver of Life Thursday – Healing (Healing Mass 6:30pm) Click here to view the Parish Mission flyer. Sr. Briege McKenna, O.S.C. was born in Ireland and entered the Sisters of St. Clare at the age of fifteen. Following her final vows and after suffering for more than three years with rheumatoid arthritis, she was transferred to her community in Tampa, Florida with the hope that the Florida sunshine would relieve her suffering. At the age of twenty-four, she was miraculously and instantaneously healed during the celebration of the Eucharist and some time later received, in prayer, the gift of healing for which she has become so widely known. Her book, " Miracles Do Happen " has been translated into many languages through out the world. Shortly after her own healing, the Lord led Sr. Briege into a ministry of healing. In prayer he told her, "You have my gift of healing. Go now and use it." It was because of this Sr. Briege began to pray with people whom the Lord in his love and mercy healed of many different kinds of sicknesses. Sr. Briege insists "I am not the one who heals. It is Jesus alone who heals us." She often refers to the Gospel encounter between the blind Bartimaeus and Jesus. The question Jesus asked Bartimaeus is the same question he asks all of us. "What do you want me to do for you?" With faith we should answer "Lord, I want to be healed." Since 1985, Sister Briege has been ministering in collaboration with Father Kevin Scallon, C.M. She is the 1988 recipient of the Poverello Award from the Franciscan University, and the 2009 recipient of the Award for Outstanding Catholic Leadership from the Catholic Leadership Institute. To learn more about Sr. Briege, visit www.sisterbriege.com . Welcome FAITH FORMATION Children's Faith Formation Over 300 children, PreK-3 through 8 th grade, will sign up this fall to learn more about Jesus and the Catholic faith. At this time, over 100 of these children have no catechist to teach them. You can help them learn and grow in faith by becoming a catechist for our Children’s Faith Formation program. As you nurture the faith of our young students, you will learn and grow as well! As one long-time catechist said, “I learn so much from the children!” We provide you with training, materials, and support. Classes begin September 10. If interested or for more information, contact Sam Di Benedetto at 626-2343 or [email protected] . You will notice that it differs from the current arrangement in that the pews are curved. The reason for this difference is that we have to meet a regulation that requires each seating position to have a corresponding kneeling position. We have looked at numerous ways of meeting this requirement satisfactorily and this is the least radical. Please take time to view this Proposed New Pew Arrangement and your feedback will greatly appreciated. The truth about who we are, how we are made, and what we are destined for is so much more beautiful! All 8th grade students and at least one parent are invited to join us for "Pure and Simple," an archdiocesan event presented by the Office of Religious Education and the Order of Lumen Gentium which proclaims these truths, on September 27 beginning with Mass at Christ the King at 5:30 PM. The evening begins with a large group presentation by Pat Arensberg, followed by guys, girls, and parent breakout sessions. This is an extra-credit opportunity for CTKCS 8th graders, but more importantly, this will prompt relevant discussions for all students as they prepare for high school, more freedom, and new influences. 8th grade students from any school are welcome to attend; all must come with at least one parent. For more information, please contact Sarah Collins at [email protected] . RCIA Are you or do you know someone who has expressed an interest in becoming Catholic or was baptized Catholic as a child, but has not celebrated the Sacraments of Confirmation and Eucharist? We offer an opportunity to come together in a small group to learn more about our faith. Sessions focus on the teachings and experience of Church and prepare to celebrate the Sacraments of Baptism, Confirmation, and Eucharist during the Easter season. You are welcome to participate in the process with your questions, your insights, and your faith story in an accepting and warm environment. For information, please contact the Church Office at 251.626.2343. Classes are on Sundays (September-Easter) from 9:30-10:50 am in the Immaculata Center. Timothy Deasy (1933 - 2016) Welcome Reverend Msgr. Timothy J. Deasy: Born in Shinaugh, Dunmanway, County Cork, Ireland, June 15, 1933 on the Feast of Corpus Christi, died peacefully on June 24, 2016. Predeceased by his parents Nora Marie (Desmond) and Jeremiah Deasy and one brother, Pat Deasy. Survived by his sisters Sr. Philomena, Sr. Eily and Sr. Teresa; brothers Denis and Fr. Fachtna (Jeremiah) Deasy; sisters-in-law Eileen and Gussie; ten nieces and nephews; and twenty-two (soon to be twenty-three) great nieces and nephews. Fr. Deasy was ordained a Roman Catholic priest at St. Patrick's Cathedral, County Carlow, Ireland, on June 7, 1958; he faithfully served the people of God of the Archdiocese of Mobile for over 58 years thereafter. He served many parishes, including St. Jude's in Montgomery; St. Margaret's in Bayou La Batre; Little Flower in Mobile; and Christ the King Parish in Daphne, where he fulfilled his ministries and resided from 1995 until his death. Fr. Deasy was a constant carrier of God's love to everyone whose lives touched his; he cherished his innumerable friends to the end. He was treasured as a good and prudent priest, pastor, confessor, and a wise counselor. So many fondly remember his hugs and kisses, his Irish charm, and his love of Jesus, of life, of his family, his Church, his sisters, his brother priests, and, of course, his abiding love for all his friends. For many families throughout the Archdiocese of Mobile, Father Deasy was "family priest," celebrating baptisms, the Eucharist, marriages, anointings, and funerals for successive generations. All who were part of his huge and very warm circle of friends mourn his passing. A funeral Mass and celebration of Father Deasy's life, with Fr. Jeremiah F. Deasy as principal celebrant, will take place at Christ the King on Friday, July 1, 2016 at 10:30 a.m. preceded by visitation at 9:30. Visitation is also scheduled for Thursday evening, June 30, 2016, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.; Office of the Dead for a Deceased Priest offered at 7:00 p.m. Burial will be at Belforest Catholic Cemetery. In lieu of flowers, memorial donations can made to the Christ the King Building Fund. I grew up in Birmingham and was an active parishioner at St. Peter the Apostle in Hoover, assisting with religious education classes, reading at morning Masses, and falling in love with Jesus through my youth group. In college, I majored in Middle Childhood and Adolescent Development at Auburn University, and I graduated in 2009 with a long-term goal of working in youth oriented non-profits or ministries. Currently, I am in my seventh year of serving at St. Michael’s high school youth group, and while guiding souls to encounter Christ is the main mission, the additional mission of authentic relationships has blessed me tenfold! I have experience teaching catechesis classes, building and leading retreats, and mentoring middle and high school youth through all kinds of life situations. I also serve on the leadership team for Biking for Babies, a non-profit dedicated to financially and spiritually supporting pregnancy resource centers through long-distance bike rides. My personal consecration through Mary and dedication to the pro-life movement renews me daily and calls me to serve as a vessel and to strive for sainthood. I am excited to see what the CTK family has been offering the community, and I feel truly blessed to be a part of your mission. Please pray for my transition and for all of the youth at Christ the King. Our journey in stewardship begins with prayer. We pray that God will change our hearts and minds to be one with Him. Our Lord began his ministry by devoting a night to prayer. The next day He called twelve ordinary men to come and be his disciples. He calls us today, through our prayer, our faith, and our actions to continue His mission and be His disciples. Take a moment to reflect and thank our Lord for the many blessing in your life. Ask and seek the guidance of the Holy Spirit as you consider how you might return to God by increasing your gifts of time, talent and treasure. RCIA Vacation Bible School Community Ministries Community Ministry Contacts FAITH FORMATION RELIGIOUS EDUCATION Adult Faith Formation Children's Faith Formation MEDIA & EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES FORMED Parish Library U.S. & World Catholic News Vatican News SACRAMENTS Baptism Reconciliation Holy Communion Confirmation Anointing of the Sick Holy Matrimony Holy Orders PERPETUAL ADORATION Perpetual Eucharistic Adoration Testimonials Become A Guardian YOUTH MINISTRY EDGE 6th-8th Grades Welcome to EDGE LIFE TEEN 9th -12th Grades Welcome to Life Teen Bathing Suit Policy Our Policies THE ALLEY Schedule PCR Applications Event & Trip Parent Consent Forms CONFIRMATION Sacrament of Confirmation ATHLETICS CYO ATHLETICS CYO Mission Athletic Prayer and Pledge Sponsorship Banners Sports Registration Join Our Coaching Team BOOSTER CLUB About Us Hoopalooza GIVING Stewardship Online Giving AmazonSmile Welcome to our Summer Seminarian Welcome We welcome our guest seminarian, Gabe Mills, from St. Meinrad Seminary and School of Theology in Indiana. Gabe is a native Mobilian and 1995 graduate of Davidson High School. Gabe credits his grandmother as the force behind his receiving the sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Eucharist at age 11 from Fr. Deasy while at Little Flower Parish, and being active in the parish through his formative years. During his young adulthood, Gabe spent 16 years working with UPS and his path with his faith life became unclear. After attending the baptism of a friend's daughter at Our Savior Parish, he was reawakened to the Catholic faith and began an active faith life at Our Savior. Gabe is entering his second year at St. Meinrad and has developed a relationship with his fellow seminarians he will be serving alongside, and they have become like family. This summer, he will be participating in One Faith One Family, working with the Marian Society, traveling with the EDGE Birmingham mission trip, and with Life Teen on their Charleston mission trip. He recently spent the weekend with our Youth Ministry students at their Panama City Retreat and is pleased to see the impact this event has in the lives of our parish youth. An avid political junkie, Constitutionalist and Patriot, outdoorsman, and a country boy at heart...stop and say hello when you see our summer seminarian around CTK and upcoming events and activities. Join us this fall as we seek to encounter the Holy Spirit in a new way through our Women’s Bible Study. All are welcome and encouraged to come. There will be child care available for all those with childrens. Study: The Wild Goose Series - http://thewildgooseisloose.com/about When: Every Tuesday from 8:00 AM -10:00 AM starting August 29th - December 12th Where: The Immaculata Center; Contact Alyssa Morisani [email protected] to reserve your study guide for $15. Help Needed: We are in need of someone to watch the nursery every Tuesday from 8:00 AM-10:00 AM from August 29th – December 12th. This is a paid position. Child Protection Certification is required. Contact Alyssa Morisani for more information. RCIA Vacation Bible School Community Ministries Community Ministry Contacts Mission: To assist parents in handing on the Catholic faith to their children in a classroom setting by promoting knowledge of our beliefs, full and active participation in the Liturgy, moral formation, and a vibrant prayer life. Time: Children in grades K-8 meet weekly on Sunday mornings for 1 hour and 15 minutes in the school classrooms. Preschool age children meet weekly on Sunday mornings for 1 hour in the Immaculata Center. All classes meet from September through April. Talent/Special Skills: Adults are needed to serve as catechists for all grade levels. High school teens are encouraged to participate as classroom assistants. All volunteers should have a love of faith and children along with a desire to fill an essential role within a Christ-centered environment. Training, materials, and support are provided. Time commitment involves weekly preparation, Sunday morning class time, and meetings as necessary. Child Protection training through the Archdiocese of Mobile is required for all adult participants. It is a sacrament of mature Christian commitment and a deepening of the baptismal gifts. Confirmation is administered by laying-on of hands and anointing with chrism accompanied by prayer. The chrism is blessed by the bishop and the bishop administers the sacrament. All baptized persons can and should be confirmed. The effect of the sacrament of Confirmation is for the individual to be sealed with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. According to the general guidelines of the Archdiocese of Mobile, a student must attend at least two academic years of religious education before receiving the sacrament of Confirmation. Since sacraments are celebrated in the parish setting, all candidates for Confirmation, no matter which academic school they attend, receive preparation in unison for the sacrament. CONFIRMATION REQUIREMENTS Confirmation preparation at Christ the King begins freshmen year of high school and concludes with the Sacrament of Confirmation during the spring of junior year. Our program is integrated into our Life Teen curriculum. Candidates must attend Life Nights on Sundays once a month and attend biannual sessions with a catechist. Teens who wish to be confirmed should register for the parish’s Confirmation Preparation Program in each of their Freshman, Sophomore and Junior years of high school. There is a $50 registration fee per family each year. For more information, contact Jan Quint , Confirmation Coordinator at [email protected] . RCIA Vacation Bible School Community Ministries Community Ministry Contacts Mission: To provide religious education and sacramental formation for parish students and their families who are preparing to receive Confirmation. Time: Meets on Sundays during the school year. The schedule is posted on the Life Teen website (www.ctkdaphne.org/youth-ministry). Talent/Special Skills: Instruction is a two-year process. Students should enroll in the Confirmation Program as they begin their ninth grade year. Adult volunteers are needed and welcome. Child Protection training through the Archdiocese of Mobile is required for all adult participants. they to win a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one. (I Corinthians 9:15) A diocese or a parish sponsors a Catholic Youth Organization as one dimension of its total ministry to youth. Athletic programs can help young people toward imperishable crowns as well as perishable ones. A parish CYO program justifies its existence and the sacrifice and expense it entails only if it allows young people to practice Christian attitudes and responsibilities. In CTK programs, emphasis rests not on the number of games won or lost, but on the participants' attitude in victory or defeat. Learning how to lose is just as important as learning how to win. Learning how to win graciously is more important than winning itself. Christ the King programs serve the needs of all youth. They enable the gifted to excel, and the less gifted to participate and improve. "Star" athletes and teams do not receive exclusive attention. Principles of fair play and sportsmanship must govern every game. Dishonesty has no place in CTK competition. Our competitors must not borrow from professional sports questionable techniques for winning at any cost. All participants should have the respect of others on their own team and the opposing team. Competitors should regard the opposition as friends, not enemies. CTK participants should have a spirit of loyalty to CYO ideals, to parish, to coach, and to the team. They should learn patience with and tolerance of those of less ability. They should feel grateful to all who make our programs happen. Speech and actions should reflect Christian values. At times, during the heat of competition, a participant may temporarily forget some rule of conduct. Prompt correction can turn even failures into learning experiences. Ultimate responsibility for the success of Christ the King programs lies with the volunteer adult participant. Adults involved in CTK must remember the program exists for the Christian growth of young people. Conduct of adults must always model Christian values and virtues. When adults forget the primary focus of CTK, the program becomes destructive. When adults remain faithful to the Christian ideals of CTK, they exercise a unique and rewarding ministry to the young with whom they come in contact. "Run to win," St. Paul advises (I Cor. 9:24). In CTK athletics, all who compete can win, if they run to win the real prize; closer union with Jesus Christ. Panama City Retreat Volunteer Opportunites LIFE TEEN 9th -12th Grades Welcome to Life Teen Bathing Suit Policy Our Policies THE ALLEY Schedule PCR Applications Event & Trip Parent Consent Forms CONFIRMATION Sacrament of Confirmation One of the most frequent questions pre-teens ask themselves is, “Who am I?” Our culture gives them a wide variety of answers, but we as the Church know only one answer matters: that they are a beloved son or daughter of God who is intentionally desired, perfectly unique, and capable of changing the world, one relationship at a time. At Christ the King’s EDGE program, our goal is to continue this conversation by providing a safe, fun place for 6th-8th graders to find a solid Catholic community, to get answers to their questions about faith, and most importantly, to experience Jesus in a profound and personal way. EDGE nights, social events, and service opportunities are all rooted in faith, fun, and fellowship. Get Involved: Students EDGE meets at The Alley (CTK’s youth house) at 810 Trione Avenue on various Wednesdays called “EDGE Nights” from 6:30-8:00 PM. (We do not serve dinner at EDGE events unless specifically noted, but we will always have snacks or dessert!) Social and service events may take us away from The Alley; check the current schedule to see what we’re up to this semester! Contact us at: Physical Address: 812 Trione Avenue; Daphne, AL 36526 Mailing Address: CTK Parish, ATTN EDGE; 711 College Ave; Daphne, AL 36526 Phone: 251-626-3992 Email: [email protected] Communication We use e-newsletters and emails to communicate with parents. Sign up for our e-newsletters and emails by clicking HERE . You can also follow us on Instagram and Facebook for pictures and other updates. We do not communicate exclusively with students; all communication is public via social media or communications with parents. Time: Training/orientation sessions are scheduled as needed. Ministers are scheduled to serve on a rotating basis according to Mass preferences. Ministers are asked to arrive 15 minutes prior to the beginning of Mass to sign-in. Talent/Special Skills: The pastor selects Candidates for Extraordinary Ministers of the Eucharist. Registration is open to all students in Kindergarten – 8 th grade. Registration will close on October 28 th . There will not be any registration extensions, so get your child signed up today! Please register at the site below: sports.ctkdaphne.org PLEASE NOTE THE 7 TH AND 8 TH GRADE DIVISIONS MAY NOT HAVE ENOUGH TO FIELD A TEAM, DUE TO MANY OF THESE STUDENTS PLAYING MIDDLE SCHOOL AT ST. MICHAEL. WE CAN COMBINE 7 TH AND 8 TH GRADE TO FORM A TEAM IF NESSECARY. AFTER REGISTRATION, IF WE DO NOT HAVE ENOUGH KIDS, I WILL REFUND EVERYONE THEIR REGISTRATION FEES. Practice will start the week of November 7th. Games will start first week of December. Game schedules will not be available until about a week before the regular season starts. Games are played in Mobile at several locations, as well as Christ the King, depending on the division. Most games will take place on Saturday, with the possibility of a few weekday games. The only division that may differ is the K5 and 1 st grade. These games will likely be played on Monday and Tuesday nights in Mobile. Once teams are formed and coaches selected, practice times and other related information will be emailed to the parents. Depending on the number of athletes that sign up in each division, certain groups may have to split into more than one team. If a group has to split into two teams, the coaches will evaluate the players, and divide teams evenly. It is imperative that teams are as equal as possible. Teams can only be split based on balance and not other factors! Boys uniforms are the same for all grades 0 - 8th! The uniform includes a reversible jersey and shorts. Make sure you have the shorts that are available for purchase during registration. They are part of our uniform and all kids need to have the same complete uniform! Girls in all grades will wear new uniforms this year. The girls basketball/volleyball jerseys have been discontinued, so all girls will have to purchase a new uniform this year. Please purchase shorts during the registration process too as they are part of the uniform! When signing your son/daughter up for sports, please be respectful of the coach's time. Coaches are volunteers and it is difficult to teach our children when they are not at practice due to other activities. Please check your schedules to make sure you can fully commit to your children being at practice and games! When selecting a basketball number for your child, they have to be legal basketball numbers! These are legal numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 00, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, and 55. The Rite of Christian Initiation of Adults (RCIA) is the process of discernment and learning in preparation for possible entry into full communion within the Catholic Church. It is offered to adults who have never been baptized, to those who have been baptized in other faith traditions, and to those who have not completed the sacraments of initiation. Participants are called to conversion through prayers, study, interaction, and discussion. Classes begin in September and meet weekly on Sundays from 9:30-10:50 am in the Immaculata Center. The Church of the Assumption was built by the early Italian colonists. Father Angelo Chiariglione, a Scalbrini missionary from Torino, Italy, was the first resident pastor (1898-1909). 1898 The Queen of Italy, Margherita of Savoy, sent a gift of rich vestments, an illuminated missal, a chalice, monstrance, candlesticks and other articles. The vestments are on display in a special case in the church vestibule today. 1925 A rectory was built under the pastorate of Father Manual Campodonico. 1937 Bishop Thomas Toolen blessed the cornerstone of a new church on October 24th, and the parish name was changed to Christ the King. Father James Loftus was the pastor at the time. This church still stands today on the Christ the King campus. It was renamed " Assumption Hall " in honor of the parish's roots, and is used for ministry and social functions daily. 1949-1950 Under the leadership of Fr. Father Denis Gray, pastor, the dream of a parochial school was realized. Christ the King Catholic School opened in September of 1950, staffed by the Sisters of Loretto (1949-1972). The Presentation Sisters from Lismore staffed the school beginning in 1972, and ending with the retirement of Sr. Maureen Nolan in 2008. 1970 The Ladies of Christ the King Parish organized the Festa Italiana. T his annual festival still takes place today at the parish. While recognizing Daphne's Italian heritage, the Festa provides funding for the Ladies Soldality, and supports the Burse Club and ACCW. 1975 The Parish Council was established and remains an active leadership body for the parish today. 1993 To better serve the growing Parish, a new church was completed, and dedicated on the Feast Day of Christ the King, November 22. 1993-Present Father Matthew O'Connor is the present pastor for Christ the King Parish. The parish currently serves over 1,900 families. The Perpetual Eucharistic Adoration Chapel , built and dedicated on March 10, 2013, has over 400 weekly committed "guardians" who dedicate an hour praying in front of our Lord Jesus. The Parish maintains over 30 ministries for Children, Youth and Adults, Development and Stewardship, Family Life, Liturgy and Worship, Outreach, and Religious Education. The Eucharist was instituted as a sacrament by Jesus at the Last Supper. The Eucharist effects union with Christ; it is nourishment for the soul and gives increase in grace. The Eucharistic celebration, the Mass, is celebrated every day at Christ the King Parish. Click to view our Mass Times . The Church draws her life from the Eucharist. This truth does not simply express a daily experience of faith, but recapitulates the heart of the mystery of the Church. FIRST HOLY COMMUNION According to the general guidelines of the Archdiocese of Mobile, a student must attend at least two academic years of religious education before receiving the sacraments of First Reconciliation and First Holy Communion. First Reconciliation and First Communion are traditionally celebrated in Grade 2. Preparation for these sacraments is offered as part of the curriculum at Christ the King Catholic School. For children who attend public or other private schools, sacramental preparation is integrated into the Sunday morning Religious Education curriculum. Parents seeking First Communion for their child(ren) who do not attend Christ the King Catholic School should contact our Director of Religious Education (DRE), Sam Di Benedetto, for details of the process. Children must be enrolled in the Sunday morning Religious Education Program at Christ the King. RCIA Vacation Bible School Community Ministries Community Ministry Contacts Mission: To work in collaboration with parish clergy, the Marian Society, and the Apostolate for Persons with Disabilities to make Christ present to those persons and families in our parish who cannot attend Sunday celebrations of the Eucharist due to illness, physical or other disability, or similar problems. Time: As needed and scheduled. Talent/Special Skills: Participants in this ministry pray and also make themselves available to perform acts of charity and the corporal and spiritual works of mercy for the homebound, as described above. Some of the participants in this ministry are authorized to distribute Holy Communion by the Archbishop or his delegate following the recommendations of out pastor and the Rite of Commissioning. We have many fun and empowering events planned for our youth throughout each year to help them grow in faith. From service projects, Life Nights, trips and retreats, we hope you find a welcoming environment to discover your faith. HOW TO KEEP UP TO DATE WITH US We have many means of communicating to our teens about what is going on. You can follow us online at these popular sights: Facebook Follow us on Facebook to get pictures of trips, updates on events, and notifications of changes. Instagram Mailchimp For everything you need to know our mailchimp email list is the best place to get the information you need for your student. WHAT TO EXPECT FROM LIFE NIGHTS AT CTK Life Nights occur every Sunday after the 4:30 PM Life Teen Mass (unless specified on the schedule). Each night begins with dinner and fellowship from 5:30-6:30 pm in The Alley. Following dinner, teens are lead in games, talks, and spiritual development until 7:30 PM. The Life Teen curriculum is used with the goal to “strengthen our teens’ Catholic identity, while rooting them firmly in Christ and His Church.” Topics range from knowledge of God through scripture and tradition, personal identity, healthy sexuality, morality, and much more. CHILD PROTECTION TRAINING Are you looking to volunteer for one of our many activities and events scheduled at CTK Life Teen this year? This includes everything from cooking on Sunday nights, chaperoning events such as bowling or trips like the March for Life. In order to do so, you must be child protection trained at least 2 weeks before the start of the event. St. Lawrence Catholic Church in Fairhope has classes the second Tuesday of each month beginning in August at 7 PM. If you wish to attend one of these, please email us at [email protected] to RSVP with what date you wish to attend. If you have already completed the initial class, please keep your training up to date online through the Archdiocese. Your retraining should be completed each August at the beginning of the school year. RCIA Vacation Bible School Community Ministries Community Ministry Contacts The ministries of Christ the King parish are organized and operate under a Commission structure. There are seven permanent Commissions. Each Commission is assigned a liaison from the Parish Council. The role of the liaison is to serve as a representative voice for the ministries in his/her Commission, as well as maintain regular contact with ministry coordinators. The following Commissions are listed below: Administration & Finance Children, Youth, & Young Adults Development & Stewardship Family Life Liturgy & Worship Outreach Religious Education Note: The organization and ministry descriptions outline the mission of each group, time commitment involved, special skills/talents needed, participation guidelines, and coordinator contact information. If you have an interest in a particular area, contact the coordinator. If you are unable to reach the coordinator, you may always contact the Parish Office directly for assistance. Christ the King welcomes your involvement! They travel from Mobile, Stockton, Spanish Fort, Daphne, Montrose, Fairhope, Point Clear, Robertsdale, Loxley, Magnolia Springs, Foley and Gulf Shores. Some are even Episcopalian, Anglican and Lutheran. For five years, over 430 committed, weekly guardians of the Blessed Sacrament have created a powerhouse of prayer by adoring Jesus at Christ the King’s Blessed Sacrament Chapel in Daphne. This beautiful outpouring of faith and love has enabled everyone the opportunity to visit Jesus anytime during the day or night on the Eastern Shore. Drop-in visits number over 1000 a week, thanks to a diligent committee of 30 men and women who work to insure all 168 weekly hours are covered with faithful prayer guardians always before the Blessed Sacrament. Mother Teresa and John Paul II were living examples of the fruits of Eucharistic Adoration. No matter how busy they were or how many important people they had to see, they made sure that they spent time with the most important Person of all: Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Every day they spent 2 to 3 hours in His Eucharistic Presence, and they told the whole world that this was where they got all their energy to do so much for God and His people. If you feel called to grow closer to Jesus and show your love to Him in a radical way, consider committing one hour a week with Him. For more information visit ctkdaphne.org or call Missy Schmidt at 251-626-7427. Click here to watch the anniversary video A five year celebration of PEA was held March 12th with a mass, dinner, and video presentation. Father Paul Zoghby was guest celebrant and speaker with over 250 in attendance. Christ the King’s Blessed Sacrament Chapel is the only perpetual adoration chapel south of Montgomery, AL and east of New Orleans, LA. “The Church and the world have a great need for Eucharistic worship. Jesus awaits us in this Sacrament of Love. Let us not refuse the time to go to meet Him in Adoration, in contemplation full of faith, and open to making amends for the serious offenses and crimes of the world. Let our Adoration never cease.” Saint Pope John Paul II Why go to Adoration? You go to Adoration to deepen your personal relationship with Jesus and grow in faith, hope, and love. Jesus will give you His peace within you as you spend time with Him. Just as you can’t be exposed to the sun without receiving its rays, neither can you come into the light and presence of Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament without receiving the divine rays of His grace, His love and His peace. What do I do during my hour? You may spend the time with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament any way you want. You may read the Bible, write in a prayer journal, bring spiritual books (or read some from our library), pray the rosary, or just sit, relax and enjoy the peace that comes from being in His Presence. You may feel you can’t pray well. Don’t let that discourage you. The fact that you come to spend time with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament pleases Him very much and is, in itself, a prayer of faith. How can I show my Love for Jesus? You can show your love by making a weekly commitment to Him. By kneeling on both knees before going into the pews, you acknowledge His True Presence. As you lift your mind and heart to Jesus during Adoration, try thinking about His suffering and believe He suffered all He did because you are very precious and worth everything to Him! “Our essential commitment in life is to grow spiritually in the climate of the Holy Eucharist.” Saint Pope John Paul II Parish Office Mailing Address 711 College Avenue Daphne, AL 36526 tel: (251) 626-2343 fax: (251) 621-1640 Map Church 1505 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Parish Library 1702 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Assumption Hall 1501 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Rectory 715 College Avenue Daphne, AL 36526 Map Immaculata Center 1601 Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map Blessed Sacrament Chapel 1505-A Main Street Daphne, AL 36526 Map The Alley 810 Trione Avenue Daphne, AL 36526 tel: (251) 626-3992 Map Copyright © Christ the King Catholic Church Login powered by eCatholic ®

Nikki Kingsley September 12 6:30 pm in the church Welcome What is the Truth? This was the burning question that led Nikki Kingsley on her journey from Islam to Christianity. Nikki’s remarkable story began in Pakistan where she was born in a Muslim family. She arrived in America at the age of thirty with her two young children, seeking freedom from an arranged marriage, and discovered the promise found in the dream called America. Nikki’s life went through a dramatic turn when she had an extraordinary series of mystical experiences. These events prompted her to question and reconsider the Muslim faith that she had practiced for 40 years. Ultimately, this led Nikki to The Truth in the person of Jesus Christ. A compelling speaker, Nikki now shares her life-changing story of faith and hope––a story of a journey from the culture, faith, and traditions of the East to the freedom of the West. She has been a guest on many Catholic shows including The Journey Home on EWTN, Ave Maria Radio, The Catholic Channel on Sirius XM, and a speaker at many Catholic conferences and retreats. Nikki Kingsley’s dynamic account of her faith journey from darkness into Light is detailed in her book, Thirst for Truth: From Mohammad to Jesus, and can be purchased on her website at nikkikingsley.com. Click HERE to for registration information. Basketball is open to all students enrolled in CTK Faith Formation or CTKCS in 1st - 8th grades. The addition of 1st graders is new this year, and we are excited to include our 1st graders in the basketball program! The girls uniforms are different this year. The 1st - 4th grade girls will continue to wear the dry-fit T-shirt type jerseys that are currently used for soccer. So, if you have one of those, no need to order a new jersey. These girls can wear any navy blue shorts, most wear Nike/Under Armour type. The 5th - 8th grade girls are wearing true basketball uniforms. These are the sleeveless jerseys currently being worn by our volleyball teams. If your daughter is playing volleyball right now, all you will need are the shorts. If you are not currently playing volleyball, you will need to order a full uniform for any girls in grades 5th - 8th. The boys in all divisions will continue to wear the same uniforms. The deadline to register is Tuesday October 30. There will be no registrations allowed after October 30. All fees must be paid by October 30 to have a jersey ordered or have your child added to a roster. Start dates for practice will be scheduled soon. In the meantime, get your registration done today! Thank you and Go Saints! Its purpose was to establish permanent scholarships for the education of men for the priesthood from the Archdiocese of Mobile. We collect funds throughout the year, but especially on BURSE Sunday, which is September 10. We present these funds to the Archbishop at the Annual ACCW Convention in the fall. These monies are then invested and used for the education of our seminarians. In 1953, the dues were set at $12.00 annually and have not been raised in 64 years. Membership is open to everyone! There are no meetings to attend; no committees to serve on; just your prayers for vocations and your financial support. Please join the Priests Burse Club to help our 14 seminarians studying for the priesthood. Chris Stewart is the co-founder of Casting Nets Ministries. He has served as youth minister, junior high religion teacher, as well as high school and college theology professor. Chris and his lovely wife, Maria, live in Wichita, KS with their seven children. Hector Molina is the CEO of Casting Nets Ministries. He is a former apologist for Catholic Answers and past Director of Evangelization for the Archdiocese of St. Louis. Hector and his lovely wife, Uki, live in St. Louis, MO with their six children. We will reassess the situation late this year to determine if classes will resume in the new year. The parish First Holy Communion which would have taken place in May has been rescheduled for Sunday, September 27 at 2:00pm. Additional information will be sent to the families of last year’s 2nd Grade students. In an effort to continue rising 2nd Grade students on their sacramental journey, 2020-2021 sacramental preparation for First Reconciliation and First Holy Communion will be offered. Additional information will be sent to the families of last year’s 1st Grade students. New families and/or new students who will be entering 2nd - 8th and have NOT received these sacraments should contact our Director of Religious Education, Sam Di Benedetto, at [email protected] or by calling our Parish Office at 251-626-2343 by October 16. Tracking Mary: Mysteries & Messages Welcome Tracking Mary: Mysteries & Messages Get your Golden Ticket To "Track" Mary All Over The World! First stop, France, then FULL STEAM AHEAD to Portugal, Mexico, Ireland & England. The Queen of Heaven Express is Leaving the Station! Discover how Mary brings us closer to Jesus through the POWER of the Rosary. Mysteries and Messages are revealed at each stop. Experience the wonder of Our Lady of Lourdes, Our Lady of Fatima, Our Lady of Guadalupe, Our Lady of Knock and Our Lady of Mount Carmel. This exciting adventure offers Union Station Skits, Full Steam Faith, Boxcar Bible, Gondola Games, Caboose Crafts, Stoker Snacks & Steam Whistle Music! Click here to download the registration form. This decision was made after much careful thought, prayer, and discussion. Our focus is on the health and safety of our children as they return to the classroom next week. Our school administrators and staff have worked extremely hard to prepare for a smooth and successful reopening. Although we are all extremely disappointed for our athletes and families, we know that CYO Sports will return stronger and better than ever before. A modified Toy Bowl is being discussed and we will have more information soon in regards to this annual 8th grade tradition. May God bless you and your families and keep you all safe and healthy. Its six short chapters contain some of the most discussed passages in the New Testament. This 4-session study examines many important themes that are still relevant in today’s Christian culture and society—the nature of marriage, the purpose and role of the Church, the preeminence of grace in God’s plan, and the reality of spiritual warfare. Email Steve Coppejans at [email protected] to register. Through the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, Dominican Friars have been proclaiming the truth of God's Word for over 800 years in order to bring Catholics into a personal encounter with the Living Christ Who reveals the unconditional love of our heavenly Father. The iMercy missiom is a unique, grace-filled evangelical moment in the life of a parish led by the Dominican Friars. This mission aims to help parishioners enter more deeply into the love of the Holy Trinity and experience God's merciful touch through the Sacraments. Officers for 2017-18 are Cheryl Miller (President), Lisa Boos (Vice President), Carol Palumbo (Secretary), Diane Sublett (Treasurer), and Sandra Hrabovsky (Member at Large). The MOSJ Outback retreat is designed for two persons to attend together, thus our retreat was composed of mothers and fathers attending with their teen sons and daughters as "campers". The campers experienced several reflective talks and outdoor activities that included a challenging high-ropes course, all designed to build, restore, and strengthen relationships with each other and with God. In order to facilitate this event, a volunteer team was formed made up of over one-hundred lay persons, largely from CTK and St. Lawrence parishes, and integrated with MOSJ volunteers from Mobile. Fr. Victor of Christ the King Parish led the campers through celebrations of the Mass and adoration, and confessions were heard with the help of six assisting priests. The Holy Spirit clearly had a large impact on both the campers and volunteers during the weekend, and it is hoped that the MOSJ Outback retreat will continue as part of our Confirmation program, with both the support of all involved, as well as those called to assist with this great event in the future. This retreat, the first ever MOSJ Outback retreat used by an entire parish as a jumpstarter for Confirmation formation, was made possible by the extreme support and generosity of the MOSJ. An experience which normally costs a parent/teen couple $295 was offered to our parishioners for only $25 a couple! Moving forward, we need your support to be able to offer this program to next year's Confirmation class and hopefully many classes to come. Consider making a donation to support this bold new ministry in our parish family by going to the following link: http://www.menofstjoseph.com , clicking "Donate Now" and marking "MOSJ Outback" before finalizing payment. Having had the MOSJ invest in our parish in such a big way, it's now our chance to "pay it forward" and keep costs low so everyone in our parish can benefit from such a dynamic, faith building experience. Dear Brothers and Sisters in the Lord, I am Thomas J. Rodi, the Archbishop of Mobile and I welcome you to take part in a Novena for the Healing of our Hearts and Home. I welcome in a special way all Catholics, Christians of other denominations and people of good will who are reading this and who live throughout the southern 28 counties of Alabama which comprise the Archdiocese of Mobile, our common home. I pray that this may be a powerful way in which we can join together as brothers and sisters, perhaps as never before, to humble ourselves before our God asking him to pour out his mercy and grace upon us to heal our hearts and home—that is, to use this trying time to draw us closer to God and to deliver us from this tragic pandemic. The term “novena” comes from the Latin word “novem” meaning “nine” and is the traditional term Catholics use for a prayer that is offered for a special intention for nine successive days. Why 9 days? Because after Jesus ascended into heaven, Mary and the apostles gathered together for nine days to pray for and await the coming of the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:3-14). Ever since the early Church received the Holy Spirit, it has been a tradition to implore God for nine consecutive days with a petition of great importance.* Tragedies, like the one we are facing, have a way of getting our attention and potentially drawing us closer to God. However this is not automatic. We have to allow ourselves to be humbled by the circumstances of life, renew our trust in God and invite him to change us for the better. Otherwise, the same tragedies may easily make us cynical and bitter leading us to resent God if not to reject him completely. Consequently, as your brother in the Lord I feel compelled to lead all of us in humbling ourselves before the only one who can completely heal our hearts and our common home—God. We just celebrated Easter, God’s triumph over sin and death. Let us not be afraid to take this unique time as an opportunity to call upon the mercy and grace of God to triumph over this pandemic and all that threatens to draw us apart from God. Let us ask him to take this cross we bear and transform it with his mercy into the peace and joy of the Resurrection. Let us pray that God may newly pour out his peace and joy over the all the world and in a particular way over all of us here in the southern half of Alabama. I have chosen to lead you in two prayers during this Novena. One is the Chaplet of Divine Mercy. It is a prayer which Jesus himself taught to St. Faustina and asked her to spread around the world. One central prayer repeats throughout the chaplet—“For the sake of his sorrowful passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world.” This is exactly what we need God to do during this time—“have mercy on us and the whole world.” The other prayer is a “Litany of Repentance” which highlights some of the ways that we have strayed from God. I have no idea why God is allowing this pandemic to affect our world. However, I do know it is an opportunity for us to slow down, realize what really matters in life and turn towards God with new fervor. So let us kneel down together ask God to heal our Hearts and our Home, so that both may be filled with the peace and joy of the Risen Lord! Sincerely in Christ, Thomas J. Rodi Archbishop of Mobile *The name of the day “Pentecost” itself is derived from the Greek word "pentecoste," meaning 50th. This is the Greek translation for the Jewish holiday, Shavu`ot, which falls 50 days after Passover. Shavu’ot is sometimes called the “Festival of Weeks,” referring to the seven weeks since Passover. Originally a harvest feast, Shavu`ot now commemorates the sealing of the Old Covenant on Mount Sinai, when the Lord revealed the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai. Every year, the Jewish people renew their acceptance of the gift of the Torah on this feast. The Resurrection occurred on the Feast of First Fruits. Pentecost (Shavu’ot) was seven weeks later. Again that’s why it’s sometimes called the “Feast of Weeks.” However, the actual dates of both were established by counting from the first Sabbath after Passover (also the day Jesus died on the Cross—Good Friday). First Fruits was the first day after the Sabbath (the first after Passover) and Pentecost was the 50th day, so there were only 49 days between First Fruits (Jesus’ Ressurection—Easter Sunday) and Pentecost. Acts 1:3 says that Jesus ascended into Heaven 40 days after His Resurrection (41 days after the Sabbath). That means Pentecost was 9 days later, not 10. In Scripture, the number 9 often marks the end, or conclusion of a matter. The arrival of the Holy Spirit on Pentecost marked the end of the Lord’s personal ministry on Earth and the beginning of his work through the Holy Spirit in his body the Church. Whereas “Pentecost” once celebrated the acceptance of God’s written law contained in the Torah, it now celebrates when God poured our his Holy Spirit upon the Church, writing his law upon our hearts. (Jer 31:33, Ez 11:19-20, Heb 10:16) In John 16:7 the Lord had told His Disciples, “I tell you the truth: It is for your good that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Counselor will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. February 2 Welcome FAITH FORMATION Two Sessions Each Day Monday, January 30 9:00 AM : Morning Mass & Mission Talk 6:30 PM: Mission Talk & Sacrament of Reconciliation Tuesday, January 31 - Wednesday, February 1 9:00 AM : Morning Mass & Mission Talk 6:30 PM: Mass & Mission Talk Thursday, February 2 9:00 AM : Morning Mass & Mission Talk 6:30 PM: Mass, Mission Talk, & Eucharistic Healing Service Themes Monday – Reconciliation [Confessions will be heard] Tuesday– The Priesthood & The Eucharist Wednesday – The Lord, The Giver of Life Thursday – Healing (Healing Mass 6:30pm) Click here to view the Parish Mission flyer. Sr. Briege McKenna, O.S.C. was born in Ireland and entered the Sisters of St. Clare at the age of fifteen. Following her final vows and after suffering for more than three years with rheumatoid arthritis, she was transferred to her community in Tampa, Florida with the hope that the Florida sunshine would relieve her suffering. At the age of twenty-four, she was miraculously and instantaneously healed during the celebration of the Eucharist and some time later received, in prayer, the gift of healing for which she has become so widely known. Her book, " Miracles Do Happen " has been translated into many languages through out the world. Shortly after her own healing, the Lord led Sr. Briege into a ministry of healing. In prayer he told her, "You have my gift of healing. Go now and use it." It was because of this Sr. Briege began to pray with people whom the Lord in his love and mercy healed of many different kinds of sicknesses. Sr. Briege insists "I am not the one who heals. It is Jesus alone who heals us." She often refers to the Gospel encounter between the blind Bartimaeus and Jesus. The question Jesus asked Bartimaeus is the same question he asks all of us. "What do you want me to do for you?" With faith we should answer "Lord, I want to be healed." Since 1985, Sister Briege has been ministering in collaboration with Father Kevin Scallon, C.M. She is the 1988 recipient of the Poverello Award from the Franciscan University, and the 2009 recipient of the Award for Outstanding Catholic Leadership from the Catholic Leadership Institute. To learn more about Sr. Briege, visit www.sisterbriege.com . Welcome FAITH FORMATION Children's Faith Formation Over 300 children, PreK-3 through 8 th grade, will sign up this fall to learn more about Jesus and the Catholic faith. At this time, over 100 of these children have no catechist to teach them. You can help them learn and grow in faith by becoming a catechist for our Children’s Faith Formation program. As you nurture the faith of our young students, you will learn and grow as well! As one long-time catechist said, “I learn so much from the children!” We provide you with training, materials, and support. Classes begin September 10. If interested or for more information, contact Sam Di Benedetto at 626-2343 or [email protected] . You will notice that it differs from the current arrangement in that the pews are curved. The reason for this difference is that we have to meet a regulation that requires each seating position to have a corresponding kneeling position. We have looked at numerous ways of meeting this requirement satisfactorily and this is the least radical. Please take time to view this Proposed New Pew Arrangement and your feedback will greatly appreciated. The truth about who we are, how we are made, and what we are destined for is so much more beautiful! All 8th grade students and at least one parent are invited to join us for "Pure and Simple," an archdiocesan event presented by the Office of Religious Education and the Order of Lumen Gentium which proclaims these truths, on September 27 beginning with Mass at Christ the King at 5:30 PM. The evening begins with a large group presentation by Pat Arensberg, followed by guys, girls, and parent breakout sessions. This is an extra-credit opportunity for CTKCS 8th graders, but more importantly, this will prompt relevant discussions for all students as they prepare for high school, more freedom, and new influences. 8th grade students from any school are welcome to attend; all must come with at least one parent. For more information, please contact Sarah Collins at [email protected] . RCIA Are you or do you know someone who has expressed an interest in becoming Catholic or was baptized Catholic as a child, but has not celebrated the Sacraments of Confirmation and Eucharist? We offer an opportunity to come together in a small group to learn more about our faith. Sessions focus on the teachings and experience of Church and prepare to celebrate the Sacraments of Baptism, Confirmation, and Eucharist during the Easter season. You are welcome to participate in the process with your questions, your insights, and your faith story in an accepting and warm environment. For information, please contact the Church Office at 251.626.2343. Classes are on Sundays (September-Easter) from 9:30-10:50 am in the Immaculata Center. Timothy Deasy (1933 - 2016) Welcome Reverend Msgr. Timothy J. Deasy: Born in Shinaugh, Dunmanway, County Cork, Ireland, June 15, 1933 on the Feast of Corpus Christi, died peacefully on June 24, 2016. Predeceased by his parents Nora Marie (Desmond) and Jeremiah Deasy and one brother, Pat Deasy. Survived by his sisters Sr. Philomena, Sr. Eily and Sr. Teresa; brothers Denis and Fr. Fachtna (Jeremiah) Deasy; sisters-in-law Eileen and Gussie; ten nieces and nephews; and twenty-two (soon to be twenty-three) great nieces and nephews. Fr. Deasy was ordained a Roman Catholic priest at St. Patrick's Cathedral, County Carlow, Ireland, on June 7, 1958; he faithfully served the people of God of the Archdiocese of Mobile for over 58 years thereafter. He served many parishes, including St. Jude's in Montgomery; St. Margaret's in Bayou La Batre; Little Flower in Mobile; and Christ the King Parish in Daphne, where he fulfilled his ministries and resided from 1995 until his death. Fr. Deasy was a constant carrier of God's love to everyone whose lives touched his; he cherished his innumerable friends to the end. He was treasured as a good and prudent priest, pastor, confessor, and a wise counselor. So many fondly remember his hugs and kisses, his Irish charm, and his love of Jesus, of life, of his family, his Church, his sisters, his brother priests, and, of course, his abiding love for all his friends. For many families throughout the Archdiocese of Mobile, Father Deasy was "family priest," celebrating baptisms, the Eucharist, marriages, anointings, and funerals for successive generations. All who were part of his huge and very warm circle of friends mourn his passing. A funeral Mass and celebration of Father Deasy's life, with Fr. Jeremiah F. Deasy as principal celebrant, will take place at Christ the King on Friday, July 1, 2016 at 10:30 a.m. preceded by visitation at 9:30. Visitation is also scheduled for Thursday evening, June 30, 2016, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.; Office of the Dead for a Deceased Priest offered at 7:00 p.m. Burial will be at Belforest Catholic Cemetery. In lieu of flowers, memorial donations can made to the Christ the King Building Fund. I grew up in Birmingham and was an active parishioner at St. Peter the Apostle in Hoover, assisting with religious education classes, reading at morning Masses, and falling in love with Jesus through my youth group. In college, I majored in Middle Childhood and Adolescent Development at Auburn University, and I graduated in 2009 with a long-term goal of working in youth oriented non-profits or ministries. Currently, I am in my seventh year of serving at St. Michael’s high school youth group, and while guiding souls to encounter Christ is the main mission, the additional mission of authentic relationships has blessed me tenfold! I have experience teaching catechesis classes, building and leading retreats, and mentoring middle and high school youth through all kinds of life situations. I also serve on the leadership team for Biking for Babies, a non-profit dedicated to financially and spiritually supporting pregnancy resource centers through long-distance bike rides. My personal consecration through Mary and dedication to the pro-life movement renews me daily and calls me to serve as a vessel and to strive for sainthood. I am excited to see what the CTK family has been offering the community, and I feel truly blessed to be a part of your mission. Please pray for my transition and for all of the youth at Christ the King. Our journey in stewardship begins with prayer. We pray that God will change our hearts and minds to be one with Him. Our Lord began his ministry by devoting a night to prayer. The next day He called twelve ordinary men to come and be his disciples. He calls us today, through our prayer, our faith, and our actions to continue His mission and be His disciples. Take a moment to reflect and thank our Lord for the many blessing in your life. Ask and seek the guidance of the Holy Spirit as you consider how you might return to God by increasing your gifts of time, talent and treasure. RCIA Vacation Bible School Community Ministries Community Ministry Contacts FAITH FORMATION RELIGIOUS EDUCATION Adult Faith Formation Children's Faith Formation MEDIA & EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES FORMED Parish Library U.S. & World Catholic News Vatican News SACRAMENTS Baptism Reconciliation Holy Communion Confirmation Anointing of the Sick Holy Matrimony Holy Orders PERPETUAL ADORATION Perpetual Eucharistic Adoration Testimonials Become A Guardian YOUTH MINISTRY EDGE 6th-8th Grades Welcome to EDGE LIFE TEEN 9th -12th Grades Welcome to Life Teen Bathing Suit Policy Our Policies THE ALLEY Schedule PCR Applications Event & Trip Parent Consent Forms CONFIRMATION Sacrament of Confirmation ATHLETICS CYO ATHLETICS CYO Mission Athletic Prayer and Pledge Sponsorship Banners Sports Registration Join Our Coaching Team BOOSTER CLUB About Us Hoopalooza GIVING Stewardship Online Giving AmazonSmile Welcome to our Summer Seminarian Welcome We welcome our guest seminarian, Gabe Mills, from St. Meinrad Seminary and School of Theology in Indiana. Gabe is a native Mobilian and 1995 graduate of Davidson High School. Gabe credits his grandmother as the force behind his receiving the sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Eucharist at age 11 from Fr. Deasy while at Little Flower Parish, and being active in the parish through his formative years. During his young adulthood, Gabe spent 16 years working with UPS and his path with his faith life became unclear. After attending the baptism of a friend's daughter at Our Savior Parish, he was reawakened to the Catholic faith and began an active faith life at Our Savior. Gabe is entering his second year at St. Meinrad and has developed a relationship with his fellow seminarians he will be serving alongside, and they have become like family. This summer, he will be participating in One Faith One Family, working with the Marian Society, traveling with the EDGE Birmingham mission trip, and with Life Teen on their Charleston mission trip. He recently spent the weekend with our Youth Ministry students at their Panama City Retreat and is pleased to see the impact this event has in the lives of our parish youth. An avid political junkie, Constitutionalist and Patriot, outdoorsman, and a country boy at heart...stop and say hello when you see our summer seminarian around CTK and upcoming events and activities. Join us this fall as we seek to encounter the Holy Spirit in a new way through our Women’s Bible Study. All are welcome and encouraged to come. There will be child care available for all those with childrens. Study: The Wild Goose Series - http://thewildgooseisloose.com/about When: Every Tuesday from 8:00 AM -10:00 AM starting August 29th - December 12th Where: The Immaculata Center; Contact Alyssa Morisani [email protected] to reserve your study guide for $15. Help Needed: We are in need of someone to watch the nursery every Tuesday from 8:00 AM-10:00 AM from August 29th – December 12th. This is a paid position. Child Protection Certification is required. Contact Alyssa Morisani for more information. Panama City Retreat Volunteer Opportunites LIFE TEEN 9th -12th Grades Welcome to Life Teen Bathing Suit Policy Our Policies THE ALLEY Schedule PCR Applications Event & Trip Parent Consent Forms CONFIRMATION Sacrament of Confirmation To help with Edge Youth Ministry, all parents/volunteers must be Child Protection Trained for the safety of both adults and students. St. Lawrence Catholic Church offers Child Protection Training the second Tuesday of each month. Those who have already taken this training must update their training online by October 1. More details can be found at: http://www.mobarch.org/resources/forms.cfm . Get Involved: Parents In the Catholic faith, parents are considered the primary educators of their children on all matters about faith. As such, we invite parents to get involved with our ministry in some capacity. We have a variety of ways to get involved! Chaperone our events. To be in compliance with the archdiocesan Safe Environment policies, we must have 1 adult (21+) chaperone to every 10 students. Donate desserts, snacks, or drinks for our EDGE Nights. Email [email protected] to donate food. Parents can also meet during our time to learn more about the topic discussed at EDGE Night; provided materials will include catechesis on the topic, provide discussion questions for parents on application to daily life, and resources for conversation with your child after EDGE Night is over. Parents wanting to facilitate this session are asked to email the Youth Minister at [email protected] . Parents can also contribute by purchasing items HERE from our Amazon Wishlist Get Involved: Young Adult Volunteers In addition to these things, our Core Team is made up of young adults (high school age and older) who are both active in their faith and excited to bring young students to Christ. The Core Team will lead small groups, participate in fun activities, and engage students. The Core Team is not made up of parents, but rather young adults or singles in the area. If you know someone who would help us build the ministry, please put in them in contact with Dillon Stein. Resources for Parents at Home Don’t know how to teach or answer your child’s question related to the faith? Use these resources: YouTube.com: Fr. Mike Schmitz and Bishop Robert Barron videos on various topics AscensionPresents.com: short videos by dynamic speakers, “providing engaging content for our audience that reflects the good, the true and the beautiful” LifeTeen.com: Blogs written by high schoolers, youth ministers, and missionaries about faith, prayer, culture, etc. Formed.org: a digital library of Catholic content. Visit www.ctkdaphne.org/formed for the parishioner password. Decision Point: Dynamic Catholics’ Confirmation prep program, which is suitable for 8 th /9 th grade catechesis. Try online at: http://dynamiccatholic.com/confirmation/view-program/ . Christ the King’s EQUIP sessions: presentations for parents on teaching the faith to your child, held monthly in Assumption Hall Be Prepared: theological presentations to better understand and be able to teach topics of the faith, such as the sacraments, Mary, objective Truth, and more. Schedule available at this link ( http://mobilefaithformation.org/%20upcoming-st-john-xxiii-catechist-program-presentations/ ). Tips for Faith Filled Parenting and Home Life Youth Involvement at the Parish There are other opportunities for students of this age to get involved with parish life. The list below does not include all activities; email [email protected] if there is another way your child would like to be involved. Altar Servers: all children in 4th grade or older who have made their First Communion can be trained to serve at Mass as an altar server. Altar servers assist the priest during Mass and are expected to fully participate in Mass as they serve. For more information on training, contact the Parish Office at [email protected] . (If your child wants to serve at the Sunday 4:30 PM Mass, email [email protected] .) Ushers: 8 th grade youth may serve as ushers for the Sunday 4:30 PM Mass, assisting with the collection. Email [email protected] if you would like to help. CYO Athletics: Cheerleading, soccer, football, tennis, golf, volleyball, and basketball are offered to provide team and athletic opportunities for parish children in grades K-8. For more information, contact Matt McDonald at [email protected] . Boy Scouts: Boys ages 11-18 are eligible to participate in Boy Scouting, which provides young boys and men with the opportunity to grow and learn through leadership development as they pledge to do their duty to God, others, and self. For more information, contact Tony Agostinelli, (251) 422-7153 or [email protected] . The Parish Library is located at 1702 Main Street . It is on the corner of Main Street and Trione Avenue in the small red brick building next to Centennial Park. (Formerly Oates Tax Service) WHEN IS IT OPEN? The Parish Library doors remain locked for safety. You may obtain access Monday-Friday from 8:00am-5:00pm and Sunday from 8:00am-1:00pm. HOW DO I OBTAIN ACCESS? Email [email protected] , call Laura Guarisco at 251-591-8282, or go pick up a keycard from the Parish Office at 711 College Ave. The Parish Library will be open and staffed by a volunteer on Sundays from 8:00am-1:00pm to allow access and assist with checkout procedures. HOW IS THE LIBRARY SET UP? The Parish Library has four collections: The Main Collection uses the Dewey Decimal system. Section 200 is Religion and most of our books are cataloged here. There is a chart on the ends of the shelves that lists the categories within the 200 section. The Audio Visual Collection contains CD and DVDs. Music, guided prayers, courses and bible studies, documentaries and movies can be found here. The Children's Collection contains books for children ages 10 and under. Books for middle schoolers on up are within the main collection. The Reference Collection contains dictionaries, encyclopedias, Vatican documents, and quite a few unique, valuable and old books dating back to the 1880’s! HOW CAN I SEARCH THE CATALOG? In the Parish Library you can use the iPad to search for titles, authors, or keywords. On your computer or smartphone, visit https://www.libib.com/u/ctkparishlibrary . HOW DO I CHECK OUT A BOOK? Send an email to [email protected] with your name, email, and phone number. A patron account will be created for you and the login information will be emailed to you. To check out a book: Login on the iPad, home computer or smartphone. Type in the book title you want to check out. Tap on the title and then click “Checkout” at the top of the page To add more books, hit X and the top right by “your items”, and follow instructions above again to find more titles. To remove a book, hit the X by the book title. When you are ready, hit “complete” at the bottom of “your items”. HOW MANY ITEMS CAN I CHECK OUT AT A TIME? 10 items. HOW LONG CAN I KEEP A BOOK? The lending period is 2 weeks. Yes, books can be renewed. HOW DO I RETURN A BOOK? Place books in the return basket, or in the outside book return on the front porch. Parish Library volunteers will check them in and reshelve them. WHAT IF I CAN”T FIND WHAT I’M LOOKING FOR? Please send any suggestions or requests to [email protected] .
